title: on_change not called for first session_state value
body:
### Summary

Streamlit 0.84 introduces an [`on_change` callback](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/stable/session_state_api.html#use-callbacks-to-update-session-state) for some interactive widgets as part of the new Session State API. I've found that the callback is not invoked for the first value (i.e., the widget's default or initial value), only for subsequent values.  

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st

def colour_changed():
    st.info(f"colour_changed: {st.session_state.colour}")

colour = st.selectbox("Colour", ["blue", "red", "yellow", "green"], key="colour", on_change=colour_changed)

st.info(f"selectbox returned: {colour}")
```

1. When the report is first run, the selectbox returns `blue` as the selected value, but the `colour_changed()` callback is not called.
2. When a different colour is selected, the selectbox returns the new colour and `colour_changed()` is called.
 
**Expected behavior:**

I believe the `on_change` callback should be called when a widget sets the initial/default value.

I'm finding that the lack of a callback for the initial value greatly complicates things because I can't depend on the callback to do stuff for every value of an interactive widget. I have to write special cases for the initial state.

This is further complicated by what seems like a bug initializing default session_state values for widgets like selectbox (see #3598).

**Actual behavior:**

The `on_change` callback is not called for a widget's initial/default value.

### Is this a regression?

No. The Session State API is new in Streamlit 0.84.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: Streamlit, version 0.84.2
- Python version: Python 3.8.11
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Just pip
- OS version: Debian buster (in a python:3.8 container)
- Browser version: Safari 14.1 on macOS Mojave 10.14.6

### Additional information

None.

title: An option to keep component values in the session state
body:
### Problem

Component values are automatically saved into the session state, but they are removed if they do not appear in the next run.
However, I sometimes want the component values to be kept in the session state if they appear at least once in some run.

For example, with the code below,
```python
import streamlit as st

page = st.radio("Page", ["page1", "page2"])

if page == "page1":
    st.text_input("Text1", key="text1")
elif page == "page2":
    st.text_input("Text2", key="text2")
```
1. The "page1" is selected on the radio at first.
2. The user inputs some text in the "Text1" text input.
3. The user changes the page to "page2".
4. The user changes the page back to "page1".
5. Then, the "Text1" text input became empty, and the corresponding field in the session state has been removed. I want it to be kept as the value input at 2.


I think this feature is demanded, for example, with multi-page apps.

### Solution

**MVP:** Some new option like `keep_value` is added to all the input components.

title: Sliders with default range value initialized using "sessionstate" becomes single value
body:
### Summary

I created two sliders with default range values. Slider X uses the "sessionstate" pattern (only setting "key"); Slider Y uses both "value" and "key" (without explicitly setting "sessionstate"). The first slider loses its range value when it is clicked and becomes a single value.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:
```
import streamlit as st
if "x" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["x"] = (3,7)
x = st.slider("x", min_value=0, max_value=10, key="x")
y = st.slider("y", min_value=0, max_value=10, value=(2,8), key="y")
st.write(st.session_state)
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Go to the main page.
2. Click on any of the sliders.
3. Click on the "x" slider (both left and right ends).

**Expected behavior:**

Expected "x" slider to maintain a range value [a, b] like "y" slider.

**Actual behavior:**

The "x" slider becomes a single value.

### Is this a regression?

No. (Caveat: I only started using Streamlit last week so I don't know if it worked in the distant past.)

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.7.0
- Python version: 3.8.10
- Using pip in a venv
- OS version: Windows 10
- Browser version: Chrome Version 99.0.4844.82

### Additional information

I have a fix which seems to work for me. In [streamlit/elements/slider,py](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py), "value" is tested for null and set to min_value or 0. This works for sliders that take in a single value but not for range value. I think it should get the saved default value in session state instead. Can someone more knowledgeable take a look and see if this is an appropriate fix? Thanks!

```
diff --git a/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py b/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py
index 92637f4b..4c582905 100644
--- a/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py
+++ b/lib/streamlit/elements/slider.py
@@ -30,7 +30,7 @@ from streamlit.state import (
     WidgetKwargs,
 )
 from .form import current_form_id
-from .utils import check_callback_rules, check_session_state_rules
+from .utils import check_callback_rules, check_session_state_rules, get_session_state
 
 
 class SliderMixin:
@@ -188,7 +188,11 @@ class SliderMixin:
 
         # Set value default.
         if value is None:
-            value = min_value if min_value is not None else 0
+            session_state = get_session_state()
+            if key in session_state:
+                value = session_state[key]
+            else:
+                value = min_value if min_value is not None else 0
 
         SUPPORTED_TYPES = {
             int: SliderProto.INT,
```

title: date_input fails to initialize from sessionstate if today's date is not in the range [min_value, max_value]
body:
### Summary

date_input fails to initialize from sessionstate if today's date is not in the range [min_value, max_value]
 
### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4884)

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
min_date = date(2029, 1, 1)
streamlit.session_state["with_min_value"] = min_date
streamlit.date_input("with_min_value", min_value=min_date, key="with_min_value")
```

or

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
max_date = date(2020, 12, 31)
streamlit.session_state["with_max_value"] = max_date
streamlit.date_input("with_max_value", max_value=max_date, key="with_max_value")
```

**Expected behavior:**
No error

**Actual behavior:**
StreamlitAPIException: The default value of <today's date> must lie between the min_value of ... and the max_value of ... inclusively.

No error is issued and date_input is correctly initialized from sessionstate if today's date lies in the range [min_value, max_value], for example:

```python
import streamlit
from datetime import date
min_date = date(2020, 1, 1)
max_date = date(2030, 12, 31)
streamlit.session_state["x"] = min_date
streamlit.date_input("x", min_value=min_date, max_value=max_date, key="x")
```

Python 3.10.4

title: Data placed in session_state is lost when debugging outside of Streamlit run
body:
### Problem
I'm not sure if this is a feature request or a regression as this behaviour did work in previous releases.

Whenever I get into more complex problems with a Streamlit app I was able to run the code in a debugger, now I run into the issue that values stored into the session_state are lost, as it appears that the session_state is reconstructed cleanly every time it is accessed.

To get around this, I have to add the following code to my app:

``` python
# When debugging locally, the session state is reconstructed with every request
st.session_state['test'] = 'present'
if 'test' not in st.session_state:
    logger.warning('Session state being replaced in debugger')
    # Replace with a simple dict for the duration of this debugging run
    st.session_state = {}
else:
    del st.session_state['test']
```

### Solution
The simplest solution is to treat code running outside of `streamlit run` as still being in a session, granted it is not associated with an HTTP session, but is still in a session for the duration of the run.

I'm more than happy for the above code to be integrated into the codebase if it helps.  Maybe with the warning message being updated to indicate that session_state is being replaced with a dict for the duration of the run outside of `streamlit run`.

### Additional context
The issue can be reproduced with this code:

```python
import streamlit as st
print(f'Version: {st.__version__}')
st.session_state['test'] = 'present'
print('Keys:')
for k, v in st.session_state.items():
    print(f'{k} = {v}')
print('Done')
```

Which produces the following output, which you will note does not display the information added to the session_state, but does raise a warning:

```
C:\Projects\example\venv\Scripts\python.exe C:/Users/etc/scratches/scratch_19.py
Version: 1.11.1
Keys:
Done
2022-10-28 10:29:56.602 WARNING streamlit.state.session_state_proxy: Session state does not function when running a script without `streamlit run`
Process finished with exit code 0
```

title: st.session_state is not preserved during page switch (with workaround)
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

In a multipage app _sometimes_ `st.session_state` is lost. Working on a test case I see that the same happens in a single page app that uses different page templates.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st

FIX_BUG=False  # <======================= change here

if "widget_option" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["widget_option"] = "option1"

if FIX_BUG:
    for k in st.session_state.keys():
        st.session_state[k] = st.session_state[k]

print("app refreshed")  # app is refreshed at every click

st.subheader("st.session_state:")
st.write(st.session_state)
chosen_page = st.radio("Choose a page:", ["PageA", "PageB", "PageC"])

if chosen_page == "PageA":
    st.header("This is PageA")
    st.selectbox("Choose an option:", ["option1", "option2", "option3", "option4"], key="widget_option")
if chosen_page == "PageB":
    st.header("This is PageB")
    st.write("We do nothing here")
if chosen_page == "PageC":
    st.header("This is PageC")
    st.write("We do nothing here")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

On the top you read `st.session_state`.

1. Leave `FIX_BUG=False`
2. On `PageA` choose any option but the default one "option1".
3. Click on `PageB`, `PageC` and again on `PageA`. You see that the content of `st.session_state` changes.
4. Clicking on `PageA` again the session status is reset and the option is "option1" again.
5. Change `FIX_BUG=True`
6. Click on the pages: the state is now preserved.

### Expected Behavior

Already explained.

The bug is fixed by copying each `st.session_state` variable on itself: I assume doing so we send them again to the Javascript frontend that will act accordingly.

Already explained.

title: Script does not always re-execute with latest params when using both session state and `get_query_params`
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

I am building a (multi-page) app in which I'd like to preserve some input parameters across the pages, but also enable for query params (url) params, for easy sharing of results. 

I have noticed that, at least with my implementation) after the first couple of clicks, one needs to interact with an UI element (dropdown, slider etc.. ) before the script is run. Otherwise, the script is run, but with the old parameters. 

The issue above is no limited to multi-page apps (I mentioned that to describe the use-case/need of the feature), but it can be reproduced for single page apps (see below).

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import streamlit as st


def update_session_state(query_params: dict, key: str, options: list = None, default_value: str = None, as_int: bool = False):
    value = query_params.get(key, [default_value])[0]
    if value == "None":
        value = None
    if as_int:
        value = int(value)
    if options is not None:
        if value not in options:
            st.error(f"Invalid value for {key}: {value}")
            st.stop()
    if key not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state[key] = value
    return value


# Get the URL parameters (query parameters)
query_params = st.experimental_get_query_params()

freq_options = [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3]
color_options = ["red", "green", "blue"]
lw_options = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

# Get the values from the URL parameters
freq = update_session_state(query_params=query_params, key="freq", options=freq_options, default_value=0, as_int=True)
color = update_session_state(query_params=query_params, key="color", options=color_options, default_value="red")
lw = update_session_state(query_params=query_params, key="lw", options=lw_options, default_value=1, as_int=True)

# Parameters
freq = st.sidebar.selectbox('Frequency', options=freq_options, index=freq_options.index(freq))
color = st.sidebar.selectbox('Color', options=color_options, index=color_options.index(color))
lw = st.sidebar.selectbox('Line width', options=lw_options, index=lw_options.index(lw))


st.header('My pretty plot')

x = np.linspace(0, 10, 100)
y = np.sin(x + freq)

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.plot(x, y, color=color, lw=lw)
st.pyplot(fig)

st.experimental_set_query_params(freq=freq, color=color, lw=lw)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the app
2. Click on the drop-downs few times
3. Observe that sometimes (very often after the 1st few clicks) you need to click on an element twice to get the full script to run. I.e. if you put a longer running process, you will noticed that the script does run, but with the previous parameters.

### Expected Behavior

The expectation is that one need a single interaction with an UI element 

### Current Behavior

There is no explicit error message related to this issue.  However I am uploading a screen-capture to demonstrate the problem. I hope this makes it clearer. 

[streamlit-app-2022-12-05-17-12-45.webm](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/18574951/205688567-d4314d6f-f107-4a40-a795-cc3314a93765.webm)


### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.14, 1.50.0, 1.50.1, 1.50.2  
- Python version: 3.9
- Operating System: MacOS 12.5.1 (Monterey)
- Browser: Firefox, Chrome
- Installed via: conda/mamba via conda-forge (also tried via pip inside conda/mamba environment, same results)

title: Persist widget state if `key` is set, even if the widget is not rendered
body:
👋 I work on developer experience for Streamlit and wanted to get some feedback on this recurring issue.

**TL;DR: Take a look at the [example app](https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/) and let us know how it impacts you, and what you think about how to fix this issue!**

**Discussion on the forums [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/keyed-widget-state-persistence-discussion-possible-fixes/37359)**

One of the current Streamlit behaviors that causes confusion for many of us is how widgets with `key='foo'` lose their session_state value when they are not rendered in a given run. It seems to come up most often with multipage apps that have some state dependency between pages, but also possible in a single page app with conditional rendering. A minimal example:

```
view = st.radio("View", ["view1", "view2"])

if view == "view1":
    st.text_input("Text1", key="text1")
    "☝️ Enter some text, then click on view2 above"
elif view == "view2":
    "☝️ Now go back to view1 and see if your text is still there"
```

I'm working with @tconkling on whether / how to update this behavior so it's more intuitive, or at least possible to get the intuitive behavior easily.

I put together a simple example app showing the behavior and linking some of the prior issues about it:
[https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/](https://keyed-widget-state-issue.streamlit.app/)

### Questions

- Do you have a full working public app where you had to hack around this (such as duplicating or using "shadow keys")? Please share with us!
- Do you have an app or use case where you rely on the current behavior (widget has `key` set but needs value to reset after not rendering), that will break if we change this? We **really** want to hear about these! Please share!

### Possible fixes

It seems like most developers we hear from find the current behavior very unintuitive, and we see a lot more use cases that have to work around this rather than benefit from it.
- Given that, should we just do a breaking change to the default behavior to persist, like most of us seem to expect?
- If so: We should still provide a path to clear keyed widget state when needed. Need to figure out how to best do this.

If not a breaking change: most proposals seem to prefer something like a `persist=` key. For example, both @whitphx and @mathcatsand propose something like this in [#4458](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4458). Thoughts on this approach, or other ideas?

title: session_state not actually changed until second page reload
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

**Summary:** 
When the multiselect widget is changed, the Streamlit page reloads from top to bottom, however the `session_state` receiving the output from the multiselect box [I.e. `session_state["myvar"] = st.multiselect(...)`] does not actually change (persistently) until the page reloads a _second_ time.  

**Details:**
I don't know if this is actually a bug, a change request, or simply something that can't be done the way I'm coding it.

When using a widget that passes it's results to session_state [I.e. `session_state["myvar"] = st.multiselect(...)`] **the page reloads from top to bottom _as soon_ as a selection is made, however the `session_state` does not actually change until the page is reloaded a _second_ time**. 

We discovered this using the `streamlit.sidebar` (however it behaves the same in any streamlit page.) We are using multiple pages in a dashboard (I.e. all our streamlit pages are in `streamlit_root/pages`) however we use a common sidebar to select what data is processed on the page. 

Previously, **if a user went to a new page, all selections on the sidebar were lost** - because the sidebar reloads from scratch. So we are attempting to use `session_state` to capture those selections, so they persist amongst all the pages. We did this by using the saved parameters within `session_state`, and then using the `session_state` to set the "default" parameter in the multiselect box (see code below.)

However, this resulted in unpredictable behavior (see image.) I was able to work around, by using `experimental_rerun()` to force a second page reload anytime the multiselect was changed - but it causes a lot of slowdown and is fragile. 

**_Is it possible for the `session_state`` to be immediately updated after selecting from a multiselect box with a single page reload?_**

![Streamlit bug report](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6683102/217595291-e6442c9c-56ac-4b12-a8e6-dd9be25c7496.png)

```Python
# Initialize (check if session_state var exists and, if not, create it)
try: garbage = st.session_state["multiselect_selections"]
except KeyError:
    st.session_state["multiselect_selections"] = []

st.write('(BEFORE) st.session_state["multiselect_selections"]: ', st.session_state["multiselect_selections"])

st.session_state["multiselect_selections"] = st.multiselect("Multiselect", 
                                                            options, 
                                                            default = st.session_state["multiselect_selections"])

st.write('(AFTER) st.session_state["multiselect_selections"]: ', st.session_state["multiselect_selections"])
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. streamlit run code.py
2. Select from the multiselect box. Now the "Before" and "After" state of the session_state variable
3. Select another options fro the multiselect box. 
4. Not the selected option disappears, but the session_state variable is finally updated after this second page reload.  

### Expected Behavior

That session_state would be immediately (persistently) updated after the single page reload triggered by making a selection from the multiselect box.

title: Session State remains after the tab is closed
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

When closing a browser tab the session state does not get wiped immediately. Expected behaviour should be that the browser close gets detected instantaneous. This makes pages with a while loop not break out of them quick enough.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import time
from datetime import datetime

def get_datetime():
    return datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")

if 'last_update' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.last_update = get_datetime()

text = st.empty()

while "last_update" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.last_update = get_datetime()
    text.write(f"last_update: {st.session_state.last_update}")
    time.sleep(1)

print("Exit because browser closed...")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the code
2. Open browser
3. Check for output, close the browser
4. Streamlit app will now take a very long time before actually printing the exit message...

### Expected Behavior

Expected behaviour would be to detect the closing of the browser quicker. Doesn't need to be instant, but it should be quicker in my opinion. Or maybe even configurable.


In the [docs ](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#caveats-and-limitations)it states the following:

> Caveats and limitations
> Here are some limitations to keep in mind when using Session State:
> 
> - Session State exists for as long as the tab is open and connected to the Streamlit server. As soon as you close the tab, everything stored in Session State is lost.

This information suggests that closign the tab / browser the session state is lost, but that is not the case.

### Current Behavior

After closing the browser tab, it will take a long time before it gets detected by Streamlit. 

### Is this a regression?

title: Stopping an asyncio producer-consumer script causes "session_state" has no key
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

When I "Stop" an asyncio producer-consumer script, I get the error: session_state has no key “xyz”, where xyz is a state that I have already initialized at the beginning of the run, and has been using during the run. In addition, a "RERUN" would pick up the state value, where it was left off. 


### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
# based on https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/best-fastest-practice-to-display-live-2d-data/19895/4
import asyncio
from datetime import datetime

import cv2
import numpy as np
import streamlit as st

QUEUE_SIZE = 1000
SIZE_IMAGE = 512


async def produce_images(queue, delay):
    while True:
        # Add bars depending on state count
        n = st.session_state.produced_images % SIZE_IMAGE
        m = st.session_state.produced_images % SIZE_IMAGE
        st.session_state.produced_images += 1

        image = np.random.random((SIZE_IMAGE, SIZE_IMAGE)).astype(np.float32)
        image[n: n + 10] = 0
        image[:, m: m + 10] = 1

        _ = await queue.put(cv2.cvtColor(image, cv2.COLOR_GRAY2BGR))
        _ = await asyncio.sleep(delay)


async def consume_images(image_placeholder, queue_size_placeholder, queue, delay):
    while True:
        image = await queue.get()
        image_placeholder.image(
            image,
            caption=f"Produced images: {st.session_state.produced_images}, "
                    f"Consumed images: {st.session_state.consumed_images}, {str(datetime.now())}\n"
        )
        queue_size_placeholder.metric(
            f"In queue (queue size is {QUEUE_SIZE})", queue.qsize()
        )
        st.session_state.consumed_images += 1
        queue.task_done()
        _ = await asyncio.sleep(delay)


async def run_app(image_placeholder, queue_size_placeholder, produce_delay, consume_delay):
    queue = asyncio.Queue(QUEUE_SIZE)
    _ = await asyncio.gather(
        produce_images(queue, produce_delay),
        consume_images(image_placeholder, queue_size_placeholder, queue, consume_delay),
    )


# ACTUAL APP #
if __name__ == "__main__":
    st.set_page_config(
        layout="wide",
        initial_sidebar_state="auto",
        page_title="Asyncio test",
        page_icon=None,
    )

    if "produced_images" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.produced_images = 0
    if "consumed_images" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.consumed_images = 0

    st.title("Hello random image!")
    produce_delay = 1 / st.sidebar.slider(
        "Produce images Frequency (img / second)", 1, 100, 10
    )
    consume_delay = 1 / st.sidebar.slider(
        "Display images Frequency (img / second)", 1, 100, 10
    )
    c1, c2 = st.columns(2)
    image_placeholder = c1.empty()
    queue_size_placeholder = c2.empty()

    asyncio.run(
        run_app(
            image_placeholder,
            queue_size_placeholder,
            produce_delay,
            consume_delay,
        )
    )
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Start the code, then click on the "Stop" button, which is to the right of "RUNNING..."
2. Note the error: AttributeError: st.session_state has no attribute "produced_images"
3. Note the number of produced images and consumed images in the caption
4. Choose to "Rerun"
5. Note that the number of produced images and consumed images continue from where they were left off.
6. Once in a rare while, the AttributeError does not appear.

### Expected Behavior

Code should stop without raising any error.

### Current Behavior

Stopping produces the error

`AttributeError: st.session_state has no attribute “produced_images”. Did you forget to initialize it? More info: [Add statefulness to apps - Streamlit Docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#initialization)
`

The strange thing is, the supposedly missing produced_images would continue counting from where it was stopped. This suggests that its value was preserved somehow, if indeed it was ever removed. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

Not that I can tell. 1.17.0 behaves this way too.

### Checklist


### Summary

The error appears while running an asynchronous chronometer/stopwatch controlled by a Streamlit interface.
The session state variables are failed to be used on the deployed version on Streamlit Cloud, while the same code works fine locally.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6818)

```Python
import asyncio
import time

import streamlit as st


async def run_chronometer(container):
    while st.session_state["chrono_running"]:
        st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = time.time()
        run_time = (
            st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] - st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"]
        )
        container.subheader(f"{run_time:.2f}")
        await asyncio.sleep(0.01)


def init_chrono():
    st.session_state["chrono_running"] = False
    st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"] = None
    st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = None


if "chrono_running" not in st.session_state:
    init_chrono()

st.header("Chronometer")
col1_run, col2_run = st.columns(2)
container = st.empty()
col1_save, col2_save = st.columns(2)

# buttons to run chronometer
with col1_run:
    if st.button("Start", use_container_width=True):
        st.session_state["chrono_start_ts"] = time.time()
        st.session_state["chrono_running"] = True
        st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"] = None

with col2_run:
    if st.button("Stop", use_container_width=True):
        st.session_state["chrono_running"] = False

# fill container when chrono is not running
if not st.session_state["chrono_running"]:
    if not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]:
        container.subheader(f"{0.0:.2f}")
    else:
        run_time = round(
            st.session_state.chrono_stop_ts - st.session_state.chrono_start_ts, 2
        )
        container.subheader(f"{run_time:.2f}")

# buttons to save chronometer result
with col1_save:
    if st.button(
        "Save",
        disabled=(not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]),
        use_container_width=True,
    ):
        st.write("Saved time:", run_time)

with col2_save:
    if st.button(
        "Delete",
        disabled=(not st.session_state["chrono_stop_ts"]),
        use_container_width=True,
    ):
        init_chrono()
        st.experimental_rerun()

# run chronometer asynchronously
asyncio.run(run_chronometer(container))
```

- Click on "Start" button again
- Click on "Stop" button again

### Expected Behavior

```
    while st.session_state["chrono_running"] and run_time < MAX_TIME - TIMESTEP_REAL:

KeyError: 'chrono_running'
```

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

title: Built-In run_query with session_state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

In conjunction with the st.experimental_connection feature, it would be nice to have sql queries that take one line of code. In addition, these queries could have an option to use existing results in a session_state if the query errors out

### Why?

These three components - the connection, the query and the error handling - all seem built out already and it would be nice to have them efficiently together as a built-in method

### How?

I'm not sure if the st.experimental_connection is included in the new method - it seems like that might be a separate first step and then step two would be something like st.run_query_with_handling(query: str, client: client, use_state: bool = True, state_name: str = None) to pull the data (client is a made-up type here, it would probably be a generic connection type defined in the class)

For st.run_query_with_handling, there could be two steps:

1. From https://docs.streamlit.io/knowledge-base/tutorials/databases/bigquery - as an example. Create a connection based on the conn_type and pull data with the query:

```
# Perform query.
# Uses st.cache_data to only rerun when the query changes or after 10 min.
@st.cache_data(ttl=600)
def run_query(query, client):
    query_job = client.query(query)
    rows_raw = query_job.result()
    # Convert to list of dicts. Required for st.cache_data to hash the return value.
    rows = [dict(row) for row in rows_raw]
    return rows
```

2. Create a wrapper that attempts the run #1 but uses existing results in st.session_state if use_state=True, else throws an error

```
def run_query_with_handling(query, client, use_state, state_name):
    try:
        output_data = query_func(query, client)
        st.session_state[state_name] = output_data
    except Exception as e:
        if state_name in st.session_state and use_state:
            log_str = (f"Unable to pull the most recent {state_name}, "
                       f"using data from the previous pull instead. "
                       f"Please check your internet connection and try "
                       f"again if necessary.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.sidebar.warning(log_str)
            output_data = st.session_state[state_name]
        else:
            log_str = (f"*******************Error*******************\n"
                       f"Could not get {state_name}. If another error is "
                       f"not present, either {state_name} doesn't exist in "
                       f"the database or the connection is broken.\n"
                       f"Error: {e}")
            st.error(log_str)
    return output_data
```

Note that the output (st.sidebar.warning and st.error) seem like nice communication with the user, but could be optional or done in another way.

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Session state doesnt clear the previous output
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

In my Streamlit application, I have implemented a feature where users can upload a text file. The workflow involves hitting a "preprocessing" button, which triggers the preprocessing of the uploaded text, and then displaying the preprocessed output. Afterward, I use this preprocessed output as input for an ML model prediction by hitting the "ML prediction" button, which subsequently displays the predictions.

I have implemented session state to store the value of preprocessing so that I can pass it to the ML model prediction step. However, I've encountered an issue where, when I upload a new file, the preprocessing output of the old file still persists alongside the new output. This behavior is unexpected, as I would expect the preprocessing output to be cleared when a new file is uploaded.

I am initialising session state still it doesnt work:
# Initialize session state
    if "preprocessed_data" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.preprocessed_data = None
    if "anomaly_output" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.anomaly_output = None 

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import requests

preprocessing_url = "http://localhost:5000/v1/preprocessing"
mlmodel_url = "http://localhost:5000/v1/mlmodel"

def main():
    # Initialize session state
    if "preprocessed_data" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.preprocessed_data = None
    if "anomaly_output" not in st.session_state:
        st.session_state.anomaly_output = None
    uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Upload a log file", type=["txt"])

        if st.button("Preprocess"):
            # Trigger the preprocessing endpoint
            response = requests.post(preprocessing_url, files={"file_name": uploaded_file})
        
            
            
            print(st.session_state.preprocessed_data)
            if response.status_code == 200:
                st.session_state.preprocessed_data = response.json()["preprocessed_log_file"]
                
                st.session_state.preprocessed_line_count =len(st.session_state.preprocessed_data)

                st.write("Preprocessed Data:")

            st.success("Preprocessing completed.")

                ml_output = ml_response.json()["ML model prediction"]
                st.session_state.preprocessed_line_count = len(st.session_state.preprocessed_data)
                st.session_state.anomaly_output = ml_output

if __name__ == "__main__":
```

### Summary

The options parameter passed to  st.selectbox is not processed at the right time. Later a change in the options parameter variable makes st.selectbox give a wrong selection.

title: Inputs are not saved in `st.session_state` when blocking happens
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

If blocking (e.g., HTTP request, sleep) happens after the button click, user inputs on `st.text_area` are not saved on `st.session_state`.
Also, if the blocking function is commented out, inputs on `st.text_area` are saved on `st.session_state` after the button click.

### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-7862)
```Python
import time

import streamlit as st


def set_state(i: int, text: str):
    st.session_state.stage = i
    st.session_state.lines = text.splitlines()


time.sleep(2)
if "stage" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.stage = 0
if st.session_state.stage == 0:
    text = st.text_area("Input your text", height=100)
    st.button(
        "Begin",
        on_click=set_state,
        args=[1, text],
    )
if st.session_state.stage == 1:
    st.title("Your text")
    for i, line in enumerate(st.session_state.lines):
        st.write(f"{i}. {line}")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Input some text on text area
2. Click `Begin` button
3. Only the title is displayed(contents of `st.session_state` are not shown)

![Screen Recording 2023-12-22 at 2 25 05](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/45100960/550da1b4-2db0-4e88-9335-abf26e6204e1)


### Expected Behavior

Inputs are saved on `st.session_state` and shown after the button click.

### Current Behavior

User inputs are not saved in `st.session_state` when the button is clicked directly. However, if the user clicks somewhere other than the button or text area before clicking the button (which causes blocking), the input is saved as expected.

### Checklist


### Summary

I have encountered an issue when using `st.session_state` in a multipage Streamlit app. The app runs without any errors in the browser, and I can successfully access and modify the  `st.session_state` values. However, in the terminal where I run the app, I get a `KeyError` indicating that the key is missing from `st.session_state`.

### Reproducible Code Example

_No response_

```
import streamlit as st

if 'my_val' not in st.session_state:
```

```
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.my_val = st.session_state.my_val + 1
```

5. Navigate between the main page and `mypage.py` in the browser.

We have partially combatted the problem by allowing the user to manually save the session state, but if our users forget, then their work since their last save is lost. title: Session State convenience function for initialization
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It'd be nice for Session State to have a convenience method for initializing it.

### Why?

Many apps have boilerplate code:
```python
if "my_key" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_key = "default_value"
```
If there are multiple keys, you might shortcut the logical test to check for one and initialize all others:
```python
if "A" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.A = "A"
    st.session_state.B = "B"
    st.session_state.C = "C"
```
If any of the keys were associated to a widget and the widget wasn't continuously rendered, you could have a situation will all keys initialized on session start, but maybe "B" or "C" got deleted later. Thus, to be really thorough, you'd need:

```python
session_init = {"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"}
for key, value in session_init.items():
    st.session_state[key] = value
```

It might be nice to have a convenience function to handle the latter:

```python
st.session_state.from_dict({"A":"A", "B":"B", "C":"C"})
```

A parameter could be used to distinguish between initializing (set if not exists), updating (dictionary merge), or full replacement (delete other keys).


### How?

Similar to how `st.query_params` is a dict-like interface with a few extra functions, `st.session_state` could get a convenience function or two.

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Preserve session state (e.g. in file, database, or localstorage)
body:

### Summary

Add a mechanism to preserve widget state or anything in `st.session_state` across sessions, e.g. by putting it into a local file, or a small database that we run alongside the Streamlit app, or an external database, or localstorage. 

### Why?

The most common use case here is being able to close the tab, come back to it later, and pick up where you left off. Also somewhat related is preserving session state across multiple pages of a multipage app (see #5813), even though I think we should find a better solution for this. 

### How?

I think we should look at whether we can find a solution that relates to syncing widget state to query params (see #302) since they basically do the same thing, just storing the values in different places. Maybe something like a parameter on every widget `sync="query_params"|"database"|"localstorage"|...`.

It would also be great to make this extensible, so that experienced devs can configure their own places where the session state should be stored (e.g. an external database).

title: Memory leak caused by session state persisting after tab closed
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

It looks like streamlit is never cleaning the session state after the tab is closed. Due to this, we're seeing memory usage increase overtime.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import numpy as np

def format_memory(mb):
    """Format memory in MB to human readable format"""
    if mb > 1024:
        return f"{mb/1024:.2f} GB"
    return f"{mb:.2f} MB"

st.title("Streamlit Memory Management Test")
st.write("This app tests how Streamlit handles large objects in session state")

# Initialize session state
if 'memory_objects' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.memory_objects = {}

if 'allocation_count' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.allocation_count = 0

# Controls
col1, col2, col3 = st.columns(3)

with col1:
    size_mb = st.slider("Object Size (MB)", 1, 500, 50)
    
with col2:
    if st.button("Allocate Memory"):
        # Create a large numpy array
        array_size = int((size_mb * 1024 * 1024) / 8)  # 8 bytes per float64
        large_array = np.random.random(array_size)
        
        # Store in session state
        key = f"object_{st.session_state.allocation_count}"
        st.session_state.memory_objects[key] = large_array
        st.session_state.allocation_count += 1
        
        st.success(f"Allocated {format_memory(size_mb)} object: {key}")
        st.rerun()

with col3:
    if st.button("Clear All Memory"):
        st.session_state.memory_objects.clear()
        st.session_state.allocation_count = 0
        st.success("Cleared all allocated objects")
        st.rerun()

# Display allocated objects
if st.session_state.memory_objects:
    st.subheader("Allocated Objects")
    
    total_size = 0
    for key, obj in st.session_state.memory_objects.items():
        obj_size = obj.nbytes / 1024 / 1024  # Convert to MB
        total_size += obj_size
        
        col1, col2, col3 = st.columns([2, 2, 1])
        with col1:
            st.write(f"**{key}**")
        with col2:
            st.write(f"{format_memory(obj_size)}")
        with col3:
            if st.button("Delete", key=f"del_{key}"):
                del st.session_state.memory_objects[key]
                st.rerun()
    
    st.metric("Total Allocated", format_memory(total_size))
else:
    st.info("No objects allocated yet")
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run this code example with `streamlit run memory_test_app.py --server.disconnectedSessionTTL=1`
2. Use the "Allocate Memory" button to create some objects.
3. Confirm (on mac os Activity Monitor) that memory usage matches "Total Allocated".
4. Delete an "Allocated Object" using the button.
5. Confirm that memory usage decreases.
6. Close the tab and wait.
7. Confirm that memory usage does not decrease.

### Expected Behavior

On step 7 streamlit deletes the session state associated with the disconnected user.

### Current Behavior

Streamlit's memory usage remains constant.

### Is this a regression?

### Debug info

title: Native support for multi-level nested keys in widget `st.session_state` assignments
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

### Problem
When building complex, dynamic forms in Streamlit (e.g., configuration builders, dynamic rows with reordering, or nested JSON editors), `st.session_state` forces developers into a flat key-value architecture. 


### Why?

Currently, if a user wants to update a nested dictionary or list, they have to use flat keys like `key=f"rep_sales_{row_id}_email"` and then write boilerplate code (either `on_change` callbacks or post-run loop reconstruction) to reassemble those flat keys back into a nested Python dictionary or data class. This leads to bloated code, higher risk of state desync (especially when reordering UI elements), and poor developer ergonomics.

### How?

### Proposed Solution
Allow the `key` parameter in input widgets to accept multi-level paths, automatically updating the deeply nested structure inside `st.session_state` when the widget value changes. Here are three potential API designs:

**Option A: State Reference Proxy (Best for IDE Type Hints & Autocomplete)**
Introduce a `st.path` proxy object or a `st.bind` method. This allows developers to use standard dictionary/attribute access—enabling IDE type hints and auto-completion—without Python prematurely evaluating the value before Streamlit sees it.
```python
# Approach 1: Path Proxy
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=st.path.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
)

# Approach 2: Object Binding (excellent for typed dataclasses)
rep = st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=st.bind(rep, "email")
)
```

**Option B: String-based Pathing**
Allow a string that represents the path. While this lacks strict type-hinting, it is highly readable and easy to implement using standard dictionary traversal.
```python
# Automatically updates st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key='representatives["sales"][2]["email"]', 
    multi_level_key=True
)
```

**Option C: Tuple/List Pathing (Pythonic Backend Approach)**
This avoids string parsing entirely, providing a clean programmatic way to define the traversal path.
```python
# Automatically updates st.session_state.representatives["sales"][2]["email"]
st.text_input(
    "Sales Rep Email", 
    key=("representatives", "sales", 2, "email")
)
```

### Expected Behavior
1. If the base key (`representatives`) does not exist in `st.session_state`, Streamlit should throw a `KeyError` (or initialize it, depending on preferred design).
2. If the path exists, when the user types in the widget, Streamlit natively traverses the nested dictionary/list and updates the final leaf node with the new widget value.
3. The widget reads its initial `value` directly from that nested path, eliminating the need to manually pass `value=st.session_state["representatives"]["sales"][2]["email"]`.

### Alternatives Considered
* **`on_change` callbacks with `kwargs`:** Developers currently do this by passing the path arguments to a callback function that mutates the dictionary. This requires declaring a separate function for every type of input, which gets incredibly tedious.
* **Third-party state wrappers:** Using external libraries or custom Python `@property` wrappers to handle the sync between flat widget keys and nested object structures. While functional, nested structures are common enough that native support would vastly improve the developer experience.

### Additional Context

As Streamlit apps grow from simple scripts into full-fledged CRUD applications and internal tools, dynamic layouts (like adding/removing rows of structured data) become the norm. Tying widget state directly to a durable, deeply nested structure rather than a flat string would solve an entire class of state-sync bugs related to dynamic UIs and list reordering.

title: Return `None` for missing `st.session_state` values
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Return `None` when accessing an uninitialized `st.session_state` value instead of raising an exception. This would remove common initialization boilerplate and make nested event data easier to consume.

### Why?

Today, initialization requires:

```python
if "foo" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

With a `None` default, this could become:

```python
if not st.session_state.foo:
    st.session_state.foo = 123
```

It could also simplify truly empty selection results for charts and dataframes while still allowing checks such as `if event_data.selection.points`.

### How?

Have missing session-state attributes resolve to `None`. The existing `AttributeDict` may already be close to this behavior; [`addict`](https://github.com/mewwts/addict) could also be useful as an implementation reference or dependency.

### Additional Context

This could be breaking for code that intentionally relies on missing values raising an exception, so compatibility and migration behavior would need careful consideration.

title: Deleting a widget's session_state key leaves the frontend showing the stale value (backend/frontend divergence for one rerun)
body: ### Checklist ### Summary Deleting a keyed widget's entry from `st.session_state` (e.g. `del st.session_state["foo"]` inside a callback) does not reset the widget, but can lead to an inconsistency between frontend and backend. The Python side returns the widget's *default* value for that run, but the frontend keeps displaying the old value, so backend and frontend disagree. On the **next** rerun the backend silently re-adopts the stale frontend value, so the deletion is effectively undone. ### Reproducible Code Example ```Python import streamlit as st text = st.text_input("Foo", value="default", key="foo") st.write("widget returned:", repr(text)) def populate(): st.session_state["foo"] = "hello" def delete(): del st.session_state["foo"] st.button("Populate", on_click=populate) st.button("Delete", on_click=delete) st.button("Noop") ``` ### Steps To Reproduce 1. Run the app. 2. Click **Populate** (callback sets `st.session_state["foo"] = "hello"`). The text input now shows `hello` and `widget returned: 'hello'`. 3. Click **Delete** (callback runs `del st.session_state["foo"]`). 4. Observe the text input on screen vs. the `widget returned:` line. 5. Click **Noop** (any interaction that triggers a plain rerun) and observe again. ### Expected Behavior The widget value in the frontent and backend should be consistent. After deleting a widget's key in session state, it should presumably fall back to its default value. ### Current Behavior - After clicking Delete, the backend returns `widget returned: "default''` , but the frontend widget still displays `"hello"`. - After the next rerun (step 5), the backend re-adopts the stale frontend value, and both show `"hello"`. ### Screenshot ### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version. ### Debug info - Streamlit version: 1.59.2 - Python version: 3.14.6 - Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 - Browser: Chromium ### Additional Information Likely related: #5442

### Current Behavior

If `r` is pressed to trigger a re-run, then the frontend updates to display `0.0` and the default value is lost.

title: Keyed persist_state=None remount can reset the UI while st.session_state[key] still holds the previous value
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

A keyed `persist_state=None` widget that has already registered, is then hidden, then shown again can render the widget default while `st.session_state[key]` still holds the previous value on that remount run. A follow-up rerun overwrites session state with the default. Unmount should reset **both** the UI and `st.session_state[key]` in the same run (#3512).

This is a follow-up to #17106 / #17093. That PR syncs delayed first mount to a leftover pre-registration user key. This issue is the already-registered remount path: unmount cleanup has dropped widget-id state, but a leftover user-key entry can leave the two sides out of sync for one run.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
import streamlit as st

st.session_state.setdefault("input2", "input 2")
st.session_state.setdefault("input3", "input 3")

select = st.selectbox("select delayed input", ["A", "B"])
if select == "A":
    value = st.text_input("input 2", key="input2")
else:
    value = st.text_input("input 3", key="input3")

st.write("widget return:", repr(value))
st.write("session_state input2:", repr(st.session_state.get("input2")))
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Load the app. Input 2 is shown on first load with `"input 2"`.
2. Switch the selectbox to B.
3. Optionally edit input 3 and press Enter.
4. Switch back to A.
5. Compare the input 2 field with the printed `st.session_state.get("input2")` value, then press `r`.

### Expected Behavior

After the registered widget remounts, both the rendered input and `st.session_state["input2"]` are the widget default (empty) on that same run. A follow-up rerun is not required to sync them.

A user key written while the widget had **never** registered remains ordinary session state: delayed first mount (and leftover-key remount after edit/hide) should still adopt that stored value on both sides. `persist_state="session"` / `"page"` (same page) should still remount the last edit.

### Current Behavior

After switching back to A (especially after editing the sibling input 3), the input 2 **field is empty** while `st.session_state.get("input2")` still prints `"input 2"` for that run. A follow-up rerun clears the printed backend as well.

Without the sibling edit, A→B→A can keep UI and backend aligned at `"input 2"`. Either interpretation of leftover keys should keep UI and printed state in sync; the #3512 unmount rule for an already-registered `persist_state=None` widget is that both sides reset in the same run.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: current develop / #17106
- Python version: 3.13
- Operating System: macOS
- Browser: Chromium (Playwright)

### Additional Information

Found during QA of https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/pull/17106#issuecomment-5813147965.

Related:

- #3512 — unmount should reset both the widget UI and the Python value in the same run
- #17093 / #17106 — delayed first mount after a leftover pre-registration user key (out of scope here)
- #12880 — identity-by-key (out of scope)

title: AppTest drops page-persistent widget state on a same-page rerun
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

AppTest loses a conditional text input's value when it is hidden and shown again with `persist_state="page"`, although the test never switches pages. The same sequence retains the value in a browser, and `persist_state="session"` works in AppTest.

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

at = AppTest.from_string("""
import streamlit as st

if st.toggle("Show", key="show"):
    st.text_input("SKU", key="sku", persist_state="page")
""").run()

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
at.text_input[0].set_value("SKU-42").run()
at.toggle[0].set_value(False).run()
print("While hidden:", repr(at.session_state["sku"]))
assert at.session_state["sku"] == "SKU-42"

at.toggle[0].set_value(True).run()
print("After showing again:", repr(at.text_input[0].value))
assert not at.exception
assert at.text_input[0].value == "SKU-42"  # Fails: actual value is "".
```

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Install Streamlit 1.65.0 in a normal Python environment: `pip install streamlit==1.65.0`.
2. Save the example as `repro_page_persistence.py` and run `python repro_page_persistence.py`. Pytest is not required.
3. Observe that the hidden value is still `SKU-42`, but the final input value is empty and the final assertion fails.
4. Change `persist_state="page"` to `persist_state="session"` and run again. The value remains `SKU-42` and the assertion passes.
5. For a browser comparison, save only the app string as `app.py`, run `streamlit run app.py`, enable Show, enter `SKU-42` and press Enter, then disable and re-enable Show. The browser retains the input value.

### Expected Behavior

Page-scoped persistence should keep the value through the hide/show sequence in AppTest because the test remains on the same page. It should return `SKU-42` after the input is shown again, matching the browser.

### Current Behavior

Reproduced on both Streamlit 1.64.0 and 1.65.0:

```text
While hidden: 'SKU-42'
After showing again: ''
AssertionError
```

There are no application exceptions in `at.exception`; the failure is the final test assertion. A browser comparison on both versions retains `SKU-42`. AppTest's `persist_state="session"` control also retains it; the default `persist_state=None` control resets it as expected.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

A previously working version has not been established. The versions tested are 1.64.0 and 1.65.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.65.0; also reproduced on 1.64.0.
- Python version: 3.14.8.
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1, arm64.
- Browser: Not required for the AppTest reproduction. Browser comparisons used the Codex in-app browser on macOS.
- Package integrity: The tested Streamlit Python files match their wheel RECORD hashes. No installed Streamlit source was modified.

### Additional Information

#### Related issues checked

- [#17119](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17119) concerns the remount of a `persist_state=None` widget and a backend/frontend mismatch. This reproduction uses explicit page persistence and works in a browser.
- [#17093](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/17093) concerns a delayed first mount after a session-state value was set. Here, the widget was mounted, edited, hidden, and remounted.
- [#16611](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/16611) concerns `AppTest.switch_page()` with a custom `url_path`. This example has no page switch or custom URL path.
- [#9128](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/9128) and [#12566](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/12566) report KeyErrors with changing widget trees. This example has no script exception and loses a page-persistent value.

I did not find an existing issue with this same reproduction.

#### Possible cause

AppTest creates a fresh PagesManager for each run. Its current page hash initially equals `""`. ScriptRunner interprets the mismatch with the target page hash as a page change and performs cleanup before resetting the context, so page-scoped persistence can be evaluated against the empty current hash.

Source links are pinned to the inspected develop commit `ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e`:

- [AppTest creates PagesManager](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/testing/v1/app_test.py#L506).
- [PagesManager initializes an empty current page hash](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/pages_manager.py#L50).
- [ScriptRunner performs page-change cleanup before context reset](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/ac7fffe6cf8474a258b2f64c96604137cfbbb37e/lib/streamlit/runtime/scriptrunner/script_runner.py#L660).

In a separate single-page diagnostic on both released versions, seeding the reconstructed runner's current page hash with the main page hash before cleanup makes this reproduction pass. It also prevents a keyed stateful tab from resetting after a child-widget interaction in AppTest. This diagnostic is evidence about the cleanup path; a complete fix must still handle real page switches correctly. The develop source was inspected, not executed.

title: Allow initialization of range slider with session state
body:
### Summary

I want to be able to create a slider and a checkbox where if the checkbox is unclicked, the slider functions as normal with some default value `val1`, but if the checkbox is clicked, the slider is locked in to a default value `val2` and resets to this value with every rerun, independent of user action. 

This functionality is possible with a standard slider using session state and key to initialize the slider value depending on the value of the checkbox, however, streamlit throws an error if you attempt to use session state to initialize a tuple of initial values for the slider (i.e. to create a range_slider). 

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:
Functionality for typical single-value slider (this works as expected):
```
import streamlit as st

val1 = 30
val2 = 70
low = 0
high = 100

use_val2 = st.checkbox('Val2?')

if use_val2:
    st.session_state.my_slider = val2
elif 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_slider = val1

slider = st.slider('My slider', min_value=low, max_value=high, key='my_slider')

```

This raises the error:
```
import streamlit as st

val1_0, val1_f = 30, 50
val2_0, val2_f = 70, 90
low = 0
high = 100

use_val2 = st.checkbox('Val2?')

if use_val2:
    st.session_state.my_slider = (val2_0, val2_f)
elif 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.my_slider = (val1_0, val1_f)

slider = st.slider('My range slider', min_value=low,
                   max_value=high, key='my_slider')

```

**Expected behavior:**

I would like the default slider range to be 30-50 and adjustable if `use_val2` is checked, and 70-90 and fixed if `use_val2` is not checked.

**Actual behavior:**
Raises  `TypeError: (30, 50) has type tuple, but expected one of: int, long, float`

### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.84.0 
- Python version: 3.8.11
- Using: pip
- OS version: Windows 10
- Browser version: Chrome

title: Selector returns invalid option if present in session_state
body:
### Summary

If the value of a selector saved in the session_state doesn't match the available options, the selector takes that value anyway even though it's no longer valid.

This can happen if the selector options are dynamic, and interacting with the dashboard changes the options.

I could check the value is one of the options every time but that shouldn't be necessary, the selector should ensure this. It would be better to ignore the invalid session_state value (possibly log it) and use the normal default.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a radio selector with options ['a', 'b', 'c'].
1. Have a button that switches to options ['a', 'b'].
2. Assert that value returned is in the list of options.
2. Selection option 'c' then press the button.
4. Get AssertionError due to value not being a valid option.

**Expected behaviour:**

Invalid option should be ignored and removed from session_state as it's no longer relevant.

**Actual behaviour:**

My code gets a selector value that's no longer valid (in my case it causes a KeyError).

Similar problem occurs with other kinds of selectors, e.g. selectbox, multiselect.

### Is this a regression?

No, new with session_state.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.85.0
- Python version: 3.7.6
- OS version: macOS 11.5
- Browser version: Safari 14.1.2

### Additional information

My dashboard does add properties to session state (taken from URL parameters) but only if not already present in the session state, used to allow users to share "deep" links that replicate the same dashboard settings.

title: Initializing default session_state value for a selectbox raises ValueError if options change
body:
### Summary

If I create a [selectbox](https://docs.streamlit.io/en/stable/api.html#streamlit.selectbox) with a key that stores the selected option in session_state and the options for the selectbox changes, Streamlit raises a `ValueError` that the previous selection is not in the new options.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import streamlit as st


list_one = ("One", ("A", "B", "C"))
list_two = ("Two", ("D", "E", "F"))


if not "list" in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.list = list_two
    st.session_state.item = list_two[1][1]


st.selectbox("List", (list_one, list_two), key="list", format_func=lambda x: x[0])
st.selectbox("Item", st.session_state.list[1], key="item", format_func=lambda x: x)
```

#### Case One (Error)

1. (Optional) Choose an option from the **Item** selectbox (the second selectbox).
2. Select **One** from the **List** selectbox (the first selectbox).

If `st.session_state.item` is initialized, in this case to `E`, when the list changes (from the first selectbox), a ValueError is raised. The report is then non-operational.

```

Traceback (most recent call last):

    widget_states = self._session_state.as_widget_states()
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 447, in as_widget_states

    states = [
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 201, in <listcomp>
    if self.get_serialized(widget_id)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 179, in get_serialized
    serialized = metadata.serializer(item.value)
  File "/root/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/elements/selectbox.py", line 113, in serialize_select_box
    return index_(opt, v)

ValueError: E is not in iterable
```

#### Case Two

If `st.session_state.item` is not initialized (comment out `st.session_state.item = list_two[1][1]`), then things work normally.

title: Exception "The truth value of a Series is ambiguous" when using Pandas row object as widget state
body:
### Summary

Note: this is a new issue when I upgraded streamlit to the current version which added session state.

Suppose I use a pandas object as the selected state for a widget like a radio button (code sample below). Then when changes occur in the widget, an exception is thrown:

```
ValueError: The truth value of a Series is ambiguous. Use a.empty, a.bool(), a.item(), a.any() or a.all().
```

### Steps to reproduce
Create a widget like a radio selector where the pandas row object (technically a `pd.Series`) is used as the selected object. Certainly one could use something like an id instead and then look up from the DataFrame, but this used to work and I had code that did things this way. It seemed convenient.

```
selected_object = st.radio("", [o for i, o in df.iterrows()], format_func=lambda o: o["someField"])
```

With the session state update, any selection of a different radio button triggers the exception, because in `session_state.py`, the `_widget_changed` method does a boolean comparison of the selected object. This isn't allowed with `pd.Series` objects.

```
    def _widget_changed(self, widget_id: str) -> bool:
        new_value = self._new_widget_state.get(widget_id)
        old_value = self._old_state.get(widget_id)
        changed: bool = new_value != old_value
        return changed
```

**Expected behavior:**

Support pd.Series objects as widget selected values.

**Actual behavior:**

Exception is thrown, application fails to function.

### Is this a regression?

Yes, worked before session state was added.

### Debug info

Seen in streamlit 0.86.0

title: Session state setting failing to propagate to frontend
body:
https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/problems-with-the-new-widget-behaviour-under-streamlit-0-89-0/17625

I investigated using the script from the post. The value seen in session state itself is being set correctly, but `should_set_frontend_state_value` incorrectly returns False. It seems like the check for `is_new_widget_value` shouldn't be part of that method. The method implementation should have been a conservative simplification of the old one that stripped out the initial value handling and separated this check from setting the value of a new widget, so I can't see why the script would have worked in 0.88, but also the current behavior is obviously incorrect.

Removing the second part of the check would make it match the obvious notion that the frontend should have its value overridden whenever the value is set in session state, and trying out this change locally appears to fix the problem.

body:
### Summary

If a widget's value is set by modifying the session state the widget does not update.

The [docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state) state

> We can set and get the value of the temperature widget by using the Session State API

### Steps to reproduce

If you take the example stated in the docs that works fine and sets the value, but only for the first run

```
import streamlit as st

if "celsius" not in st.session_state:
    # set the initial default value of the slider widget
    st.session_state.celsius = 50.0

st.slider(
    "Temperature in Celsius",
    min_value=-100.0,
    max_value=100.0,
    key="celsius"
)

# This will get the value of the slider widget
st.write(st.session_state.celsius)
```
If you modify the session state before the widget is "initialized" the GUI does not update,

e.g. with the following example:

```

import datetime

def cbk_text_input():
    st.write('callback text')
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

def cbk_slider():
    st.write('callback slider')
    st.write(datetime.datetime.now())

if 'id_input' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['id_input'] = ''

if 'my_slider' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state['my_slider'] = 5

st.session_state['id_input'] = 'sdf'
st.session_state['my_slider'] = 50

                            key='id_input',

                         min_value=0,
                         max_value=100,
                         value=4,
                         step=5,
                         on_change=cbk_slider)

answer
st.session_state['id_input']
x
st.session_state['my_slider']
```
But I would expect the widget to also reflect a "manual" change to the session state.
I would have expected the slider to move and the text box to change its content.

no clue

title: stop() messes the link between session_state and widget appearances
body:
### Summary

Setting widget default values through session_state works. However, a momentary interruption (`st.stop()`) between the initialization of the session state and the initialization of the widget generates a bug in the appearance of widgets.
* The default value of the widget is well set,
* but the widget visually display `min_value` instead of that value


### Steps to reproduce

Below is a minimal reproducible example. It is a slight modification of the [celsius example](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#session-state-and-widget-state-association).
```python
import streamlit as st

if "celsius" not in st.session_state:
    # set the initial default value of the slider widget
    st.session_state.celsius = 50.0

st.session_state["stop"] = st.selectbox(label="Select 'no'", options=["yes", "no"])
if st.session_state["stop"] == "yes":
    st.stop()

slider_value = st.slider(
    "Temperature in Celsius",
    min_value=-100.0,
    max_value=100.0,
    key="celsius"
)
st.write(f"session state: {st.session_state.celsius}")
st.write(f"value of widget: {slider_value}")
st.write("That's weird: visually, the slider is set to -100!")
```

Note that the problem does not appear if `st.stop()` is put at the beginning of the code.

title: Inconsistent session state behavior when used with widgets
body:
### Summary

Session state in Streamlit 0.89.0 to 1.5.0 has a strange behavior when bound to widgets (`key` parameter).

### Steps to reproduce

#### First case

1. In the same script run, initialize a session state item, and display a widget bound to it.
2. Make the widget disappear (by unchecking a checkbox for instance).
3. Reload with `R`. **ISSUE: Session state item doesn't exist anymore.**
4. Reload again multiple times. **ISSUE: Session state is cleared every other run.**

#### Second case

1. In a first script run, initialize a session state item.
2. In a second run, display a widget bound to the previous session state item (by checking a checkbox for instance).  
    **ISSUE: Widget does not take value from session state.**
3. Change widget value, it updates the session state item correctly.
4. Make the widget disappear.
5. Reload with `R`. **ISSUE: Session state item resets to its initial value**.

#### Code snippet

Feel free to compare the following script behavior with Streamlit 0.88.0 (working session state) and Streamlit 1.5.0. Both cases are implemented.

```python
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

c1, c2 = st.columns(2)

with c1:
    st.subheader("Widget session state item 1")
    st.write("Session state and widget setup in the same run.")
    st.write("When widget disappear, session state item is cleared every other run.")

    with st.echo(code_location="below"):
        if "widget_bound" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.widget_bound = "hello"
            st.success(f"Item added: {st.session_state.widget_bound}")
        else:
            st.info(f"Item exists already: {st.session_state.widget_bound}")

        # Displayed from the beginning by default
        if st.checkbox("Display widget", True):
            st.text_input("Some widget", key="widget_bound")

with c2:
    st.subheader("Widget session state item 2")
    st.write("Session state setup first, then widget in another run.")
    st.write("Widget does not get value initial value from session state.")

    with st.echo(code_location="below"):
        if "widget_unbound" not in st.session_state:
            st.session_state.widget_unbound = "hello"
            st.success(f"Item added: {st.session_state.widget_unbound}")
        else:
            st.info(f"Item exists already: {st.session_state.widget_unbound}")

        # Displayed after session state initialization
        if st.checkbox("Display widget", False):
            st.text_input("Some widget", key="widget_unbound")
```

### Is this a regression?

Yes, session state with widgets worked as expected from version 0.86.0 to 0.88.0.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.89.0 to 1.5.0
- Python version: 3.8.6 (pyenv)

title: widget state not synced between multiple pages
body:
### Summary

I noticed that the widget state for inputs with same keys is not synced when switching pages.
This comes a bit surprising with the [documented](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/get-started/multipage-apps#notes) and observed  shared session state.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4989)

Code snippet:

- index.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write(st.session_state)
```
- pages/a.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```
- pages/b.py
```py
import streamlit as st

st.write('st.session_state', st.session_state)
st.text_input('inp', key='shared_input')
```

(Please provide a code snippet! This will help expedite us finding and solving the problem.)

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. Run `streamlit run index.py`
2. Click on Page A
3. Enter text into input
4. Click on Page B
5. See preserved session state, but empty input widget

**Expected behavior:**

Widgets with same user keys should be synced when switching pages.

**Actual behavior:**

Widget state goes out-of-sync with session state.

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
no

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.11.0
- Python version: 3.10.0
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex? Nope
- OS version: Fedora 36
- Browser version: Brave/Chrome

### Additional information

Current **workaround** is to explicitly copy over the previous' page widget state into the session state to populate widgets using the same keys.
```py
st.session_state.update(st.session_state)
```

To not force widgets to invalid selections, our actually used workaround only does so on page navigation.

```py
if ctx := get_script_run_ctx():
    new_page = ctx.page_script_hash
else:
    logger.warning('Missing streamlit context')
    new_page = 'unknown'

old_page = st.session_state.get('_page_script_hash')

if new_page != old_page:
    # https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4989
    st.session_state.update(st.session_state)

st.session_state['_page_script_hash'] = new_page
```

Also see:
- [Session State and Widget State association](https://docs.streamlit.io/library/advanced-features/session-state#session-state-and-widget-state-association)
- [An option to keep component values in the session state · Issue #4458 · streamlit/streamlit](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4458)
- [Preserve widget state when a widget disappears from the page (demoed via Multipage Apps) · Issue #5813](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/5813).

title: Reset widget state by deleting the session state value
body:
### Summary

Deleting the key of a selectbox widget from the session only leads to a half reset of it. The output variable is reset to the default, but the actual widget display is stuck on the previous selection.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-5442)

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

selected_option = st.selectbox('Option', ['A', 'B', 'C', 'D', 'E'], key = 'selection_box')
st.write(f"Selected option: {selected_option }")

if st.button('Reset selection'):
    del st.session_state['selection_box']
    st.experimental_rerun()
```
Select an option other than A, confirm that it is printed out below. "Reset" the widget with pressing the button.

**Expected behavior:**

That the selection widget goes back to selecting option A and prints that as the "selected_option" variable.

**Actual behavior:**

The selectbox is still stuck on the previous selection but the variable "selected_option" has been updated back to the default giving a missmatch between widget state and widget output.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/22641888/192976098-92c48da4-19f5-4938-9c33-2e53596c59a0.png)
With pressing rerun the variable "selected_option" get's set again to the previously selected option so that the widget state and output are identical, but it will never fully be reset to the default option.

### Is this a regression?

No, it is the same in 1.9, 1.10, 1.11 and 1.12. I didn't go back further in versions.

### Debug info
