title: st.experimental_get_query_params() does not work with Always Rerun
body:
### Summary

When using st.experimental_get_query_params() and Always Rerun on source code changes, the query params will return an empty dict after a couple of code changes. This is frustrating for any app that uses query params because you can't just turn on Always Rerun or your app breaks after a couple code changes. 

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st

st.set_page_config(layout="wide")

st.text('1')
st.write(st.experimental_get_query_params())
```

If applicable, please provide the steps we should take to reproduce the bug:

1. `streamlit run app.py`
2. Open your browser to the URL with some query params like http://localhost:8501?param=something
3. Edit the '1' to a '2'
4. In browser pre 'r' for rerun. 
5. The query params should be correct. Rerun seems to work fine. 
6. Now edit the '2' to a '3' in the code. 
7. This time press 'a' to always rerun. 
8. The first time the query params should be correct. 
9. Edit '3' to '4'. 
10. The query params will now come back as an empty dict `{}`

**Expected behavior:**

The query params should not change, the URL in the browser is still there an correct with `param=something`

**Actual behavior:**

An empty dict is returned. 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2138258/148153409-c67198dd-d58c-4b94-b5c4-919c5674fe1e.png)


### Is this a regression?

Not sure if this ever worked. 

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.3.1
- Python version: 3.7.6
- Using virtualenv
- OS version: 10.15.7
- Browser version: Chrome 96.0.4664.110

### Additional information

I did some printing in the codebase and a fix is to replace: 
```
client_state.query_string = self._client_state.query_string
```
with:
```
 client_state.query_string = self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string
```
here: https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L184
to look like: 
```
    client_state = ClientState()
    client_state.query_string = self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string
    widget_states = self._session_state.as_widget_states()
    client_state.widget_states.widgets.extend(widget_states)
    self.on_event.send(ScriptRunnerEvent.SHUTDOWN, client_state=client_state)
```
otherwise the self._client_state seems to never be set in the first place with the query string. If you print out `self._client_state.query_string` versus `self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx.query_string` you'll see that the former is empty upon the first run whereas the latter is filled with the query params after the first run. The reason is the ctx is set here https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L273 but the self._client_state is not. 

The SHUTDOWN signal triggered by `self.on_event.send`, therefore, sets into the ReportSession the empty query string to the ReportSession's self._client_state [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/report_session.py#L354) which is then used to create the ScriptRunner in the next rerun when a file changes [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/report_session.py#L575).  

It seems better to use the `self._script_thread.streamlit_report_ctx` value as well because `experimental_set_query_params()` can set the query_string in the ctx during script running, so the self._client_state is also incorrect in that scenario. The proposed fix seems to correct both issues of Always Run not working and `experimental_set_query_params()` being not passing it's query_string back to the ReportSession either. 

I don't believe the widget_states in the ClientState proto have the same issue because they are being set on each script run [here](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/d15594b8e9f8d420af75e92cb909f52392992a75/lib/streamlit/script_runner.py#L349) as the self._session_state which is used to fill in the ClientState returned from ScriptRunner on shutdown.

title: Non-invertible `format_func` breaks widget serialization/caching
body:
### Summary

An app with an input widget whose options can take different sets of values (e.g. select box with `["Alice", "Bob"]` and `["Amy", "Barry"]` as below) seems to cache the widget state based only on the `format_func`'ed option values, rather than the raw values.   In example below, the app initially serializes the select box `Selectbox(["Alice", "Bob"])` as `Selectbox(["A", "B"])`. When the select box changes to `Selectbox(["Amy", "Barry"])`, it is still serialized as `Selectbox(["A", "B"])`, leading to streamlit trying to find `"Amy"` in the cached `Selectbox(["Alice", "Bob"])`, thus resulting in the observed `ValueError`.

I assume this is due to the serialization logic in https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/f8d6827f4f478700bdd07cc75f3131c63ee71079/lib/streamlit/elements/selectbox.py#L107 in the generation of the SelectBoxProto, which only uses the `format_func`'ed view of the options and thus has unexpected behavior for non-invertible `format_func`'s.

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```
import streamlit as st
options_1 = ["Alice", "Bob"]
options_2 = ["Amy", "Barry"]

if st.checkbox("Swap names"):
    options = options_1
else:
    options = options_2

st.write("Choose between {} and {} by first letter".format(*options))

name = st.selectbox("First letter", options, format_func=lambda x: x[0])

st.write(f"You chose {name}")

```

Click "Swap names".

**Expected behavior:**

App doesn't crash.
 
**Actual behavior:**

```

    states = [
  File "/home/devon/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 213, in <listcomp>
    if self.get_serialized(widget_id)
  File "/home/devon/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/state/session_state.py", line 189, in get_serialized
    serialized = metadata.serializer(item.value)
  File "/home/devon/.local/lib/python3.8/site-packages/streamlit/elements/selectbox.py", line 120, in serialize_select_box
    return index_(opt, v)

    raise ValueError("{} is not in iterable".format(str(x)))

```

### Is this a regression?

No.

title: Query parameters are not read on first run in streamlit cloud
body:
### Summary

When deploying an app to streamlit cloud, I discovered that query parameters behaved differently than in my local development version. In my app, I set a default value for a field in `session_state` if it is not provided through query parameters, but I could never get the query parameters to work on the cloud deployment. After some debugging, I found that query parameters always seem to be empty on the first run of the app in streamlit cloud.
 
### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import logging

import streamlit as st

params = st.experimental_get_query_params()
logging.info(f"{params=}")
if "my-field" not in params:
    st.session_state["MY_FIELD"] = "some default value"

params_second = st.experimental_get_query_params()
if "MY_FIELD" in st.session_state:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=} {st.session_state['MY_FIELD']=}")
else:
    logging.info(f"{params_second=}")

st.write(params)
```
Open app in browser with query parameter like this `?my-field=0`

**Localhost behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:47:46.902 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:47:46.903 params_second={'my-field': ['0']}
```

**Streamlit cloud behavior:**

```
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.085 params_second={'timestamp': ['1643716924162']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params={'my-field': ['0']}
2022-02-01 12:02:06.319 params_second={'my-field': ['0']} st.session_state['MY_FIELD']='some default value'
```

You can see that the app seems to run twice on streamlit cloud. In the first run the query parameters are empty (except a `timestamp`). The default value will get set in the session_state. In the second run the query parameters are present but the default value has already been set.

### Is this a regression?

I don't know.

### Debug info

- Streamlit, version 1.4.0
- Python 3.9.10
- Browser version: Chrome Version 97.0.4692.99

title: st.plotly_chart() overrides user interaction by unwantedly resetting camera
body:
### Summary

Plotly 3D animations normally allow user interactions (zoom, rotating figure with the mouse) to persist across frames.
Some animations (e.g. go.Mesh3d with frames) reset the camera despite the Streamlit user changing its params.

### Steps to reproduce

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-4653)

![dXQum](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/70368164/165344941-fc4cd84e-5a1a-4bae-bccf-d1f22af7ef9a.gif)

This animation displays frames containing each 32 go.Mesh3d() traces (one per facet of the soccer ball).

Steps (see GIF above):

1. interact with the figure (zoom and/or rotating it with the mouse)
2. either click the Plotly figure button 'Play' or move the slider with the mouse
3. watch the figure camera reset itself unwantedly

Can provide MRE if needed.

**Expected behavior:**

The camera position changed by the user persists across frames.

**Actual behavior:**

The camera position changed by the user gets reset to its initial value. Even using [`uirevision`](https://plotly.com/python/reference/layout/#layout-uirevision)


### Is this a regression?

No

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.8.1
- Python version: 3.10.0
- OS version: Ubuntu 20.04 (WSL2)
- Browser version: Chrome 100

### Additional information

This issue has been mentioned in a number of threads on SO and plotly Community, see e.g. [here](https://community.plotly.com/t/preserving-ui-state-like-zoom-in-dcc-graph-with-uirevision-with-dash/15793) and [here](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/58345327/prevent-camera-resetting-after-plotting-with-plotly-python). It is suggested [here](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/how-to-keep-the-view-of-a-plotly-plot-when-changing-a-parameter/2952) in the Streamlit forum that using session state might do the trick, but I couldn't make it work.
Last, I have noticed that commenting out `layout="wide"` from `st.set_page_config` avoids this bug but only between the Streamlit session start and the first interaction with a Streamlit widget

title: ability to make JS calls from within the user session inside the browser
body:
### Problem

A Streamlit app I'm working on needs to be able to send Ajax requests from within the web browser to communicate  with some APIs that rely on CORS and needs the request to be sent from the app user directly and can't go over the server itself.

My current workaround is a very crude custom component that renders a button in itself that does the Ajax call and then sends the JSON response from the API back to python, the problem with that is, the button won't conform with the Streamlit theme the user sets for themselves and always look out of place.
I tried putting the custom component behind a Streamlit button so it gets rendered and thus sends the Ajax requests once button is pressed but that didn't work out at all.

### Solution

**MVP:** What's the smallest possible solution that would get 80% of the problem out of the way?

A way to send Ajax requests from within the web app by clicking a button that returns a JSON object that can be used within the Python code. Perhaps it could be done by triggering the Ajax call via a button and then writing the response to into the session_state.

**Possible additions:** What are other things that could be added to the MVP over time to make it better?

A possible addition would be to also allow normal get/post requests from within the browsers.

Would that be possible or is this too specific of a use case?

title: multiselect reset to defaults behavior is inconsistent
body:
I use a selectbox to select a main option and based on this selection the multiselect widget should be reset to the default options for this main option. This works as expected if the two main options have different defaults:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1093567/167023633-38c7c845-5507-4463-893d-fbce94ac4f8c.mov

```python
options = {"a": ["1", "2", "3"], "b": ["4", "5", "6"]}
main_option = st.sidebar.selectbox("A or B", sorted(options))
other_options = st.sidebar.multiselect("numbers", ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"], 
                                       default=sorted(options[main_option]))
```
However, the same does not work when the main options have the same defaults; in this case the previous selection is kept:

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1093567/167024103-79776c38-3f35-485b-b408-a7d1134933d6.mov


```python
options = {"a": ["1", "2", "3"], "b": ["1", "2", "3"]}
main_option = st.sidebar.selectbox("A or B", sorted(options))
other_options = st.sidebar.multiselect("numbers", ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"], 
                                       default=sorted(options[main_option]))
```

**Expected behavior:**

Every time the script is rerun due to a change somewhere, the multiselect should be reset to its defaults.

**Actual behavior:**

The reset behavior is inconsistent depending on whether the previous selection is part of the defaults or not.

### Is this a regression?

Don't know

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.8.1
- Python version: 3.10.2
- Using PyEnv and PipEnv
- OS version: macOS 12.3.1
- Browser version: Chrome 100.0.4896.127 (Official Build) (arm64)

### Additional information

In another issue something similar was referenced as [desired behavior](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/1259#issuecomment-606897345), not sure if I would agree, especially since the case where something should be kept can probably be fixed with the `session_state`, while in my case I did not find a way to get the correct reset behavior, even if I stored and then manually deleted the values from the `session_state`, so it's also very intransparent where the old selected values are actually stored if the `session_state` is empty...

title: Data persists between reruns of streamlit app (including reruns of node & python servers)
body:
### Summary

Type here a clear and concise description of the bug. Aim for 2-3 sentences.

I am building a pretty simple streamlit component that displays a button that calls a function from an external node module. The function from the node module interacts with a browser extension that returns a value upon user interaction, this value is then displayed in Streamlit.

The problem:
When I ran the app for the first time, everything worked fine, but then after clicking the button again, Streamlit is skipping the user interaction part (which is in the My_Component.tsx file) and automatically outputs the initial value. This happens even after I restart the node & streamlit servers.



### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:
Note: the ctx.reset() and session_state.clear() are there just for debugging, but they don't actually change anything about the problem. While the context & session state are then empty or at least don't include the persisted data, when I console.log the data from the streamlit component, it's still there.

```
_my_component = components.declare_component(
    "my_component",
    url="http://localhost:3001"
)


def my_component(label, key=None):
    ctx = get_script_run_ctx()
    ctx.reset()
    st.write(ctx)
    st.session_state.clear()
    st.write(st.session_state)
    return _my_component(label=label, default="0", key=key)

st.session_state.clear()
st.session_state.return_value = my_component(label="my", key="component")
st.write(st.session_state)
```

(Please provide a code snippet! This will help expedite us finding and solving the problem.)

The WIP component code is also available ![here](https://github.com/AlgoveraAI/streamlit-metamask/tree/q3-develop).

**Expected behavior:**

Every time I click the button, I want to trigger an authentication request from the user, the user needs to interact with the popup (in this case a Metamask signature request) and only then should the streamlit app output a string (in this case wallet address). If the user doesn't authenticate, we should get an error or some specified output message.

**Actual behavior:**

The component worked on the very first run, but after that, even when I stop the node & python servers, the authentication step is always skipped and the component prints the string from the first interaciton (the initial wallet address that was connected, although on subsequent reruns, the wallet is clearly not connected).

### Is this a regression?

That is, did this use to work the way you expected in the past?
yes

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.5.0
- Python version: 3.10
- Using Conda
- OS version: macOS Mojave
- Browser version: Brave 1.37

title: Multiselect widget loses selected values when list of options is large

title: Joining user threads
body:
### Problem

This request is related to #1792. There is no mechanism currently to join user issued threads from the script runner thread.

### Solution

**MVP:** 

After some digging, I think the simplest way to address this is to kill all active threads stored in the session state during `AppSession.shutdown`. (I don't know where the cached variables are stored, but something similar for those as well.)

Below is my minimal working example, monkey patching `AppSession.shutdown`:

```python
import streamlit as st
import time
import asyncio
import threading

# monkey patch to kill all active threads stored in the session state
from streamlit.runtime.app_session import AppSession

_shutdown = None

def app_session_shutdown(appsession):
    # kill all threads in the session state
    states = appsession._session_state
    for key in states:
        val = states[key]
        if isinstance(val, threading.Thread) and val.is_alive() and not val.isDaemon():
            val.join()

    # run the normal AppSession.shutdown
    _shutdown(appsession)

if AppSession.shutdown != app_session_shutdown:
    _shutdown = AppSession.shutdown
    AppSession.shutdown = app_session_shutdown

# END MONKEY PATCHING

class AsyncThread(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
        self.started = threading.Event()
        self.join_req = None

    def get_time(self, delay=1):
        """user function interface"""
        future = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(self._get_time(delay), self.loop)
        return future.result()  # Wait for the result:

    async def _get_time(self, delay):
        """user function implementation"""
        await asyncio.sleep(delay)
        return time.strftime("%X")

    def start(self) -> None:
        """waits until thread is running"""
        super().start()
        self.started.wait()

    def join(self):
        """release main()"""
        if self.join_req:
            self.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self.join_req.set)
        super().join()

    def run(self):
        """Thread function. Run until join_req is set"""

        async def main():
            self.loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
            self.started.set()
            self.join_req = asyncio.Event()
            await self.join_req.wait()

        asyncio.run(main())

if "async_thread" not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state["async_thread"] = th = AsyncThread()
    th.start()

st.text(st.session_state["async_thread"].get_time())
st.button("Click bottom to update the time")
```


When applied on the source, the relevant lines in `app_session_shutdown()` should be placed in [L203 of `runtime/app_session.py`](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/7ec02a14bddbf866e36b1fe24a25afe72a5975b1/lib/streamlit/runtime/app_session.py#L203)

**Preferred solution:** 

Introduce the `blinker.signal` mechanism (which is already being used for the `ScriptRunner` class) in `AppSession` to allow users to assign arbitrary shutdown event handlers.

title: Sliders ignore user input if value argument changes
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

When I create a slider that uses `value=50.` every time, it works as expected. But if I create a slider that uses `value=np.random.uniform(0,100)`, it ignores all user input. Specifically, when I move the slider, it immediately jumps to a random location and returns that random value. The values I select are not returned from the slider at any point.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import numpy as np
import streamlit as st

r1 = st.slider("Fixed initial value", min_value=0.0, max_value=100.0, value=50.0)
print(f"{r1=}")
r2 = st.slider(
    "Random initial value",
    min_value=0.0,
    max_value=100.0,
    value=np.random.uniform(0, 100),
)
print(f"{r2=}")
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Run the above code. 
2. Move the bottom slider.
3. Move the bottom slider again.

### Expected Behavior

When I move the bottom slider to, say, zero, the slider should return zero.

Probably the slider should also ignore the `value` argument, remaining where the user set it, if a user has set a different value, but this is arguable.

### Current Behavior

When I move the bottom slider, it jumps to a random value and returns that random value. 

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.15.2
- Python version: 3.10.6
- Operating System: Ubuntu Linux
- Browser: Firefox
- Virtual environment: plain venv


### Additional Information

This arose when I was trying to write code that extracted the default value from an external class. The code was meant to read the value from the class, pass it to the slider, and save the value selected by the user into the class. Because of the above behaviour, the value only changes every other time I try to set it. Presumably if there's a new `value` passed in I only get back that answer, but if the `value` is the same as last time I can successfully select a new value?

```python
thing.j = st.slider(..., value=thing.j)
```
Here `thing` is a persistent singleton and the reading and writing are protected by a lock.

To work around this I suppose I need to record in `session_state` what the default value is and be sure to supply the same value every time?

title: Composable/reusable component API for larger apps
body:
### Problem

When an application becomes larger, we would like to split the code into some parts and compose them to build the entire application.

Let me show a toy example below.
This app shows item cards that contain widgets that users can click.
The "favorite" checkbox states are managed and accessed via the Session State, and the recommendation score (similarity to other favorite items) is calculated for each item and it controls the content of the item card.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

import streamlit as st

@dataclass
class Item:
    id: str
    name: str


items = [
    Item(id="foo", name="Foo"),
    Item(id="bar", name="Bar"),
    Item(id="baz", name="Baz"),
    Item(id="qux", name="Qux"),
]


def calc_similarity(id: str, other_favorites: list[str]) -> float:
    # XXX: Replace with some awesome algorithm!!!
    a = set("".join(other_favorites))
    if len(a) == 0:
        return 0
    b = set(id)
    return len(a.intersection(b)) / len(a)

def render_card(item: Item, favorites: list[str]):
    similarity = calc_similarity(item.id, favorites)

    with st.container():
        st.text(item.name)
        if st.button("Buy this item", key=f"{item.id}:buy_button"):
            st.text("Thank you!")
        st.checkbox("Mark favorite", key=f"{item.id}:fav_check")
        if similarity > 0.5:
            st.text("This item matches your preference!")

favorite_ids = [k.split(":")[0] for k, v in st.session_state.items() if k.endswith("fav_check") and v]

for item in items:
    other_favorite_ids = [i for i in favorite_ids if i != item.id]
    render_card(item, other_favorite_ids)
```

The key concept here is to encapsulate the card contents in the `render_card()` function.
We often take this strategy of encapsulation when building large applications like data catalog that repeats items in the same form or data dashboard that renders many similar figures or graphs (the [Components Hub](https://components.streamlit.app/) app is a good example).

The problem here is that, generally, input components such as `st.button` or `st.checkbox` requires the `key` argument when the labels are not unique in an app.
So we have to make the unique keys in this app by concatenating the ID of each item and an arbitrary string like `f"{item.id}:fav_check"`.
Key uniqueness is also necessary to access each value via the Session State.
However, when the number of child widgets in a item card becomes bigger, this boilerplate code is hard to write and manage. Also, as these keys are just simple strings, we have to parse the concatenated string to restore the original data such as the item ID and the child widget key.

### Solution

I think a new API like the following example may improve the situation.
```python
@st.component  # NEW!
def item_card(item: Item, favorites: list[str]):
    similarity = calc_similarity(item.id, favorites)

    with st.container():
        st.text(item.name)
        st.image(item.img_url)
        if st.button("Buy this item"):  # No key required explicitly if reference via the key isn't needed.
            st.text("Thank you!")
        st.checkbox("Mark favorite", key="fav_check")  # This key doesn't need to be unique globally.
        if similarity > 0.5:
            st.text("This item matches your preference!")

for item in items:
    other_favorite_ids = [i for i in favorite_ids if i != item.id]
    render_card(item, other_favorite_ids, key=item.id)
```

In this concept, the function decorated with `st.component` has an isolated namespace for the `key`, so that we no longer have to take care of the duplication of the `key` of the repeated items in the global scope.

To access the widget values through the Session State, the key might be nested like `st.session_state[parent_component_key][child_widget_key]`.

In addition to the namespace isolation, such encapsulation may have other benefits.
For example, it might be possible to memoize this function to reduce the computational and rendering cost.
In the example above, we can skip the execution of `calc_similarity()` when the input does not change.

If such composability/modulability is introduced, we could more easily build larger apps by composing isolated child components in many nested levels.

I think Streamlit's execution model is like React, so it also can import other React's concepts such as component composability like this example.

title: Support isLoading on buttons
body:
### Problem

Today, to inform a user that something is happening (and that we can't compute when it'll complete), we can put a st.spinner() somewhere on the page. We also would like to disable the button, so the user don't retrigger the behaviour by frustration (else we need to handle it in code). The most efficient way in the current architecture is to use a combination of session state and callback on buttons to handle these behaviours (click on button > disable button > show spinner in the same st.container() as button OR replace button > display result and restore button)

Whilst good in most cases, it is not as elegant as combining all this with the isLoading behaviour of base web. See : https://baseweb.design/components/button/ and toggle Primary.

### Solution

**MVP:** A new argument can be added to the `st.button()` api : `loading` or `is_loading`, set to `False` by default. Setting it to `True` would toggle the behaviour to show a spinner instead of the original label. Loading animation should display well on Primary, Secondary and ideally Tertiary (to cover all cases)  (see #6414) styles.

**Possible additions:** Adding a small text input next to the spinner would be great for customizability (🔥Computing, 🤞 Hang on...) , and added with another argument `loading_message`, put to the right of the spinner.


### Additional context

title: Support controlled components like React whose values can be controlled via passed arguments
body:
### Problem For example, when we want to make 2 sliders synchronized, we may write code like this: ```python if "value" not in st.session_state: st.session_state.value = 0 def on_change(key): st.session_state.value = st.session_state[key] st.slider("Slider1", key="slider1", value=st.session_state.value, on_change=on_change, args=("slider1",)) st.slider("Slider2", key="slider2", value=st.session_state.value, on_change=on_change, args=("slider2",)) ``` However, it has a problem that the grabbing state on a slider is cancelled after rerun. ![CleanShot 2023-04-26 at 13 48 53](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3135397/234565995-d36aa837-65a4-4e89-92cd-ae143e9d5887.gif) It may be because, the `value` argument of `st.slider` is > The value of the slider when it first renders. and the slider component is rerendered when the `value` is changed. The correct code without this problem is like this, where the value is controlled via the session state: ```python if "value1" not in st.session_state: st.session_state.value1 = 0 if "value2" not in st.session_state: st.session_state.value2 = 0 def on_change1(): st.session_state.value2 = st.session_state.value1 def on_change2(): st.session_state.value1 = st.session_state.value2 st.slider("Slider1", key="value1", value=0, on_change=on_change1) st.slider("Slider2", key="value2", value=0, on_change=on_change2) ``` However, it looks a little bit verbose, and the number of combinations would explode easily. For example, in React, we can write similar code like this, and it works as expected: ```jsx function Foo() { const [value, setValue] = useState(0); return (
setValue(parseInt(e.target.value, 10))} /> setValue(parseInt(e.target.value, 10))} />
) } ``` So, I want Streamlit to support controlled components like React, so that we can control the **current**, not the initial value of the component, through a passed argument. ### Additional context The synced slider example above looked trivial though, I think there are some similar cases. For example, my [color theme editor app](https://github.com/whitphx/streamlit-theme-editor) has several components whose values should be synchronized. --- Community voting on feature requests enables the Streamlit team to understand which features are most important to our users. **If you'd like the Streamlit team to prioritize this feature request, please use the 👍 (thumbs up emoji) reaction in response to the initial post.**

body:
### Problem

We want to use URL query parameters to control whether the sidebar is collapsed, so we can embed Streamlit into Confluence pages without the sidebar. This used to work but now fails because you can't call `st.experimental_get_query_params` before calling `st.set_page_config`.

### Solution

Provide a way for users to set the initial sidebar state, e.g. with a URL parameter, or a way to get URL parameters that can be done before calling `st.set_page_config`, or a way to collapse the sidebar after configuring the page.

### Additional context

We're also using `st.experimental_get_query_params` for deep-linking by adding session state as query parameters, so that users can share the address with others and they will see the dashboard in the same state. We will feel happier when this is no longer an experimental feature.

title: Support multiple sidebars and put the page list into a separated sidebar
body:
### Problem

It's easy to get overcrowded when sharing a single sidebar.

I need three separated sidebars for:

1. page tools (original sidebar)
2. a long list for multiple apps/pages
3. a shared/public config panel across pages (e.g. editing `session_state`, showing ENV variables...)

### Solution

The UI may look like this (three icons):

![Screenshot 2023-06-05 at 14 24 02](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/804308/dc840b69-ea0d-469f-87c8-9b9464119347)

Pseudo code in `app.py` (main page):

```py
import streamlit as st

def provide_page_list():
    ...
    
# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_left_bar_item("page", "page.png", provide_page_list)


def shared_panel():
    ...
    return ["pages/about.py", "pages/monitor.py",  ...]

# name, icon_image, callback_function
st.add_right_bar_item("tool", "tool.png", shared_panel)
```

A `right_bar_item` is also a sidebar, but it shows at the right side.

The `add_left_bar_item` / `add_right_bar_item` will be shared across pages, since the traditional sidebar is used for current page only.

You can open one left sidebar and one right sidebar at the same time, but you can only open one sidebar for each side (it means that when you open the second left sidebar, it will close the first one).

title: st.data_editor is not stateful when styling disabled columns
body:
### Checklist


### Summary

This is a bug [reported in the forum](https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/using-st-data-editor-on-dataframes-that-have-styled-columns/44752). The underlying issue is how the data editor determines equivalency of pandas stylers.

If you have a dataframe with two columns (A and B) with column B both styled and disabled, the data editor will correctly show the styled column B and editable column A. However, the widget will not be stateful unless the styler object passed to it is coming from session state. It needs to be identically the same object in memory for the data editor to be stateful. Redefining the same styler element will be viewed as "different" and cause the data editor to be recreated from scratch.

Thanks to DGR from the forum for an executable code snippet. I've modified it here to highlight the issue:

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"A": [1, 2, 3, 4], "B": [1, 2, 3, 4]})
styled_df = df.style.format({"B": "{:.2f}€"})

if 'df' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = df
    st.session_state.styled_df = styled_df

col1, col2 = st.columns(2)

with col1:
    st.subheader("Styled df in session state")
    st.data_editor(
        st.session_state.styled_df,
        key="display",
        disabled=("B"),
    )

with col2:
    st.subheader("Styled df redefined each rerun")
    st.data_editor(
        styled_df,
        key="display2",
        disabled=("B"),
    )

st.write(st.session_state.styled_df == styled_df)
st.write("Streamlit version: ", st.__version__)
```


### Steps To Reproduce

1. Change a value in column A on the left.
2. See it updates correctly.
3. Change a value in column A on the right.
4. See the widget reset and not update correctly.

### Expected Behavior

Two equivalently defined styler objects should be viewed as "the same" for the purposes of the widget reconnecting to an instance on the front end. The data editor should be stateful.

### Current Behavior

The data editor is not stateful when passed equivalent styler objects between reruns; it requires identical pointers to the same styler object.

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.23.1
- Python version: 3.11
- Pandas version: 2.0.2
- Operating System: Windows 10
- Browser: Edge
- Virtual environment: Conda


### Additional Information

@LukasMasuch

body:
### Checklist


### Summary

st.data_editor does not contain added rows when it is created out of a dataframe from a json loaded with st.file_uploader. The rows are visualized, but not accessible in the data_editor object.

- deleting rows works fine
- added rows are accessible in a roundabout way via st.session_state["key_of_data_editor"]

A forum post on this issue can be found here: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/adding-rows-in-st-data-editor-from-loaded-dataframe/46439

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/113979448/b057b729-9807-47fb-bb6c-4a4487628db5)
[Saved_dataframe.txt](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/files/12031019/Saved_dataframe.txt)


### Reproducible Code Example

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-6995)

```Python
import streamlit as st
import pandas as pd


def onchange():
    st.session_state.file_changed = True

# initialize Dataframe and state variables
if 'df' not in st.session_state:
    st.session_state.df = pd.DataFrame({'name': ["1", "2"], 'Type': None})
    st.session_state.file_changed = False
    st.session_state.loaded = False

# file upload
uploaded_file = st.file_uploader("Choose a file", on_change=onchange)
if uploaded_file is not None:
    st.session_state.loaded = True
    if st.session_state.file_changed == True:
        st.session_state.df = pd.read_json(uploaded_file)
        st.session_state.file_changed = False

# create editable Dataframe
edited_df = st.data_editor(
    st.session_state.df,
    num_rows="dynamic",
    hide_index=True,  # this is relevant for the workaround, not sure about the bug
    key='demo_df'
)

# bug: edited_df only contains the entire visualized content including added rows, if it was not loaded from file
# deleted rows are treated correctly though
st.write("edited_df:")
st.write(edited_df)
# path to workaround: the changes (from the loaded file) are visible in the df in session_state when accessed by key
st.write(st.session_state["demo_df"])
```

`if st.session_state.loaded:

else:

st.write(fixed_df)`

data_editor should behave the same no matter where the dataframe used to create it comes from.

edited_df does not contain rows added in the GUI when it was created from a dataframe loaded via st.file_uploader

title: st.progress with recurring timer, key and callback
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Setting the st.progress in a loop when doing something slow is certainly intuitive, but how about giving the slider a timer, a callback and a key. 

The timer could also be a new standalone invisible widget, e.g., st.timer(interval=1000, callback=my_callback, ...)

This would allow for example to scan an API endpoint for progress in the callback ,and set the progress value there. This would make more sense if you won't run the entire python script on any change in the frontend. I think you could still use your paradigm for interactive widgets, where the user is giving some input through the frontend, but for a progress update, which is a "pure output" widget, you could use a different paradigm (i.e. the python script won't be re-run). 

I think this new paradigm (special case for pure output widgets) won't overcomplicate your nice model, you will just have to explain that the "pure output" and "input" widgets behave differently. 

Without this, you either have stay in a loop updating the progress, thus blocking the python script (which has as a side effect that other widgets are dimmed), or to use st.experimental_rerun with some st.session_state and implement state-machines (certainly doable, but messier). 

Thank you for your time, and keep going with your great framework! I'm a big fan!

### Why?

Think about a REST API which provides an endpoint for starting a long task, and a second endpoint where you can get the progress of the long running task. 

Without a timer, you either have stay in a loop querying the API and updating the progress, thus blocking the python script (which has as a side effect that it dims other output), or to use st.experimental_rerun with some st.session_state and implement state-machines (certainly doable, but messier). 

### How?

st.timer(interval=1000, callback=on_tick)

Ideally no python script rerun on timer callback or progress update. 

### Additional Context

The SelectSlider ElementTree node has a `.set_value()` function, which one would presume takes ANY type of value as long as it matches the type with which the `st.select_slider` widget was initialized. This is not the case -- it only accepts strings.

> Note: I suspect this also happens for Multiselect but I haven't tested it yet.

### Reproducible Code Example

```Python
def test_select_slider_with_int():
    at = AppTest.from_string(
        """
    import streamlit as st

    selected = st.select_slider("My Slider", [1, 2, 3], value=2)
    """
    ).run()
    select_slider = at.select_slider[0]
    assert select_slider.value == 2

    # THIS SEEMS TO BE A BUG WITH AppTest WHERE ONE IS 
    # REQUIRED TO CONVERT THE SET VALUE INTO A STRING
    at = select_slider.set_value(2).run()
```


### Steps To Reproduce

Put the code above into `lib/tests/streamlit/elements/select_slider_test.py` or any other py-testable file with the appropriate imports.

### Expected Behavior

`select_slider.set_value(2).run()` should not cause an exception to be raised, because the `st.select_slider` widget is defined with a list of `int`s.

### Current Behavior

ValueError within the `.run()` call while AppTest is assembling the widget states. 
```

    w = get_widget_state(node)

    v = serde.serialize(self.value)

iterable = ['1', '2', '3'], x = 2

    def index_(iterable: Iterable[_Value], x: _Value) -> int:
        """Return zero-based index of the first item whose value is equal to x.
        Raises a ValueError if there is no such item.
    
        We need a custom implementation instead of the built-in list .index() to
        be compatible with NumPy array and Pandas Series.
    
        Parameters
        ----------
        iterable : list, tuple, numpy.ndarray, pandas.Series
        x : Any

        for i, value in enumerate(iterable):
            if x == value:
```

title: Add callbacks to sidebar page navigation and `st.page_link`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

When navigating to a different page, it is useful to update `st.session_state`. 

### Why?

We have a multipage app with the following structure:
1. the first page allows the user to make a selection and then run calculations on that selection
2. the selection is stored in `session_state`

When users navigate from page 1 to page 2 and then return to page 1, they expect page 1 to start in it's initial state. In fact, I have seen users press the link to page 1 (from page 1) in order to undo the selection. 

### How?

A callback argument to `st.page_link` would be great. For sidebar navigation, I do not have a definite proposal. It could be an option to `st.page_config`, but that would feel off, since `page_config` is not global to all the pages. Probably best would be to have access to a per app singleton object: `application`, which can have a method `add_switch_page_callback` or `on_page_switch`.

### Additional Context

Similar issues arise because components have no callbacks.

title: New component: `st.drawer` as a dismissable container
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Streamlit has expanded its layout options, which compound on each others to create complex application user flows beyond the single page, top to bottom interaction. 

As `st.dialog` is coming along, and `st.popover` merged, most types of surfaces are being covered by streamlit, except the drawer concept, which is a dismissable container sliding from the right of the screen on demand, which blocks the screen from the side without masking the context, can be used as an information surface, for continuous interactions (like LLM Chat), or for form input. 

### Why?

`st.sidebar`, which is the current closest equivalent has been very useful to have a permanent set of widget independent of the main window context but fall short when

- The interface has to be conditional, it requires more `session_state `trickery to redraw the sidebar
- The navigation gets rich, and the sidebar should have only a few other static elements but not a full form entry / sub interface

Thus, the sidebar and drawer concepts may overlap for simple usage, but are very different in practice and we would beneficiate from a better separation of duty 

Gitlab makes a good example of using a rich navigation sidebar to the left hand side, and drawers for Gitlab Duo AI Chat, or to input CI Variables

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/3c830664-12c6-4b8a-8e91-8192c326a05d)

![image](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/assets/97103608/5bd212a0-f31a-4f73-b4f4-3fca85374585)


### How?

The [Base Web](https://baseweb.design/components/drawer/) component is a starting point.

The main behaviours between the background and drawer I can refine in a first round are : 

- _Focused_ : The background is frozen, the user must exit using a default exit button. Clicking on the background does not exit the drawer (as it leads to different input errors). A drawer is always exitable. The background gets slightly greyed out, to ensure the drawer is in focus but remains readable
- _Scrollable_ : The background can be scrolled. This ensures that the user can retain a mental image of where they are in the UX Flow of the app.
- _Form Like (Optional)_ : The developer should be able to set a condition which closes the drawer, similar to how `st.form_submit_button` allows to exit the form. Perhaps we could reuse behaviours, and a form could be nested within a drawer, upon submission it closes the drawer.

With only those basic behaviour we can address most use cases:

1. A one-shot configuration (i.e. use a drawer to make a request, drawer closes and request shows up in main app area)
2. A continuous data entry, where the drawer remains open whilst the user makes several input (i.e. add multiple records)
3. An information/documentation panel with little interactions, but potentially rich display elements
4. A chat like interface on demand, a la copilot or gitlab duo chat.

On the python end, `st.drawer` should be similar syntaxically to st.dialog and st.popover to ease on the cognitive load, meaning

```python
with st.drawer("Open Drawer"):
   ...

```

Should call the drawer to expand, clicking away or on a well visible close/exit button should close the drawer.

### Additional Context

_No response_

title: Add an `on_complete` or `on_focus_leave` for `st.data_editor` to debounce saving state
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

I'm looking for a trigger for `data_editor` that fires only when the user leaves focus of the table, rather than on every change to every cell. Kind of like a debounce to the table.

### Why?

I want to use the data editor in a multi page application and keep it persisted across pages in an intuitive way.

The naive thought would be 
```py
st.session_state["my_data"] = st.data_editor(st.session_state["my_data"], ...)
```
You cant do this because it causes the table to reset whenever you change a value. If I add a row, it then gets removed when I move to a new cell/click out.

There is a `key` and `on_change` but that has the same issue, wherein I can do something like
```py
def _update_state():
    base_df = se.session_state["my_data"].copy()
    edited_rows = st.session_state.get("ed", {})
    added = edited_rows.get("added_rows", [])
    edited = edited_rows.get("edited_rows", {})
    deleted_idxs = edited_rows.get("deleted_rows", [])
    if deleted_idxs:
        base_df = base_df.drop(deleted_idxs)
    for idx, changes in edited.items():
        for col, changed_value in changes.items():
            base_df.loc[idx, col] = changed_value
    for new_row in added:
        ... # add new rows
    if not st.session_state["my_data"].equals(base_df):
        st.session_state["my_data"] = base_df

st.data_editor(st.session_state["my_data"], key="ed", on_change=_update_state)
```

but when you update `my_data` in session state, it breaks out the users focus from the data editing table.



### How?

What i'd love is a trigger `on_complete` or `on_focus_remove` where the user actively chooses to click out of the table, _then_ the trigger fires. In that world, my `_update_state` would actually work perfectly.

### Additional Context

This relates to https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/7749 but i wanted to formalize the request

title: Move st.app_state further up in the roadmap
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

State management has been by far the most common complaint about Streamlit online when I was comparing various dashboarding libraries. There is a mention of `st.app_state` in the roadmap, which is great, but there is no timeline of when it will go into development / be finished. I would like to suggest that this `st.app_state` be given a definite date, ideally as soon as possible. 

I also saw that NoSQL database mentioned, I would suggest considering pickling the entire `st.session_state`. It'll be faster and more robust in almost every way -- there is no network trip to the database, no need to occupy an extra process running the database, no lookups, and minimal serialization. It also works for any data type, and as far as speed goes for large binaries, what you wouldn't pickle you wouldn't store in a NoSQL database anyway. 

I would further propose that as opposed to having to register data in `st.session_state`, have all state data be registered by default. This comes from personal experience where my code is bloated by 50-100% from having to save and load every single thing into `session_state`, and it's usually the exception that I have a truly stateless component. 

### Why?

Given how many people the app reruns issue impacts, and literally everyone handling their own way, it would seem logical to make this a priority. From looking at the up-coming todos, I think st.app_state has the highest impact, as measured by
```
no. of hours saved * no. of streamlit users affected / development hour
```

For example, I have a custom component dedicated to state management, which saves and loads yaml, among other things,  and I'm almost certain that I'm not the only one. And as mentioned, almost 50% of my code is related to checking, saving to, or loading from `st.session_data`, and I've spent more time than I want on thinking about caching.

### How?

I'm open to however it's planned to be developed, but it seems wrong to me that an app would rerun the script from top to bottom on every interaction as a foundation. But, I'm unfamiliar with how streamlit works under the hood, so what I say could be misguided. 

Having developed in Angular and React, my two cents is to adopt some kind of model-view-controller (MVC) framework in the background. Generally events / interactions should only propagate up to the component it affects, and no further. My understanding is that these components are usually modelled as trees. 

How this can be done without changing the API is more difficult, and above my pay-grade. 

### Additional Context

To me `st.session_state` and various caching mechanisms are bandaid solutions that puts off dealing with the much larger issue related to the app rerunning from top to bottom on every interaction. In other words, if streamlit was stateful by default, there wouldn't be a need for session states and far fewer occasions where caching is needed. I'm not sure the proposed `st.app_state` is intended to address that underlying issue of the app rerunning on each interaction, as at face value it sounds like what will hopefully be the last fix -- which is ok if that's the best we can get.

title: st.selectbox could be typed so that it always returns T unless the index is None (etc)
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, the return type of [selectbox](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/1b73b444fe118b65f20957166f216b0e83a23e00/lib/streamlit/elements/widgets/selectbox.py#L79) is `T | None`. As far as I know, the only way for selectbox to return `None` is if `index` is `None` or if `OptionSequence[T]` is empty (`OptionSequence[]`?). These conditions could be added to the type signature of selectbox using [overloads](https://mypy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/more_types.html#function-overloading), and then in my program I wouldn't have to `assert` or `str` the results of every st.selectbox. There would be one or two overloads that returned `None | T` and one that returned just `T`. NoReturn could also possibly be added to the return type union, because if you choose an invalid index the function will error and never return.

Or maybe this goal is doomed. My project uses a lot of https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/api-reference/caching-and-state/st.session_state#session-state-and-widget-state-association stuff like:

```python
import streamlit as st
st.session_state.name = "Max"
st.selectbox("Your name", ["Sam", "Max"], key="name")
```

and I don't really know how to account for this in static typing, because the program could set the session_state value of the widget to `None`.

Furthermore, it may be unavoidable that there's always the possibility of an error in rendering, or suchlike, that would cause the widget to return None. I don't know enough to say.

So, I think this typing feature is desirable, but it may be impossible.


### Why?

Currently, whenever I use a selectbox in my typed project, I have to deal with the type union somehow each time, even though the result should always be of a certain type, which is a bit annoying.

I'm just wondering if is possible to **disable** reruning on user resize window or interact with application (froze interface) when heavy tasks are running, with global thread state or similar.

We have a Front (streamlit) with connection with other micro-services (FastAPIs), and I know we can change to an event service approach, but is more suitable for us in this moment, to have an option in streamlit to not reruning the application if it isrunning specific tasks in the script thread.

So when my application (Streamlit) sends a request streaming the response of a micro-service, if I a user cliks or resizes, or interacts with other component in the interface, streamlit it raises a StopException, because has to rerun, but my streaming response is still running and updating the interface, we don't want to rerun or take care of user interaction until specific process ends.

A functional approach can be to have a global lock, that all the code inside this block, cannot be stoppable until it ends, so interactions when enter on this blocks are blocked or enqueued, or give to the developer the control to manage this rerun.

title: Return values from fragments
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It would be great to be able to use the return value of an `st.experimental_fragment` decorated function. I know this is not currently possible but I just wanted to highlight how much of a game changer this would be.

### Why?

* The ability to have form-like blocks within an app that can have internal logic
* Improving typing by avoiding having to use session state (untyped) as a workaround for the lack of return values
* For the most part fragments are best used as terminal state in the app, whereas this would enable them to be used at intermediate steps
* Streamlit app performance would be greatly improved (and simpler to manage) because we don't have to carefully cache everything that comes before a function. Even caching is not free and it would help reduce the memory usage of streamlit apps. 

### How?

I would expect the functionality to be largely similar but with the additional feature that during a whole-app re-run the caller of the fragment has access to the return value of the function. When just the fragment updates there's an implicit `st.stop()` after the fragment has run so there's no need to worry about what happens to the return value then.  

### Additional Context

title: Non-Blocking Async Progress Bar
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

An async progress bar that allows one to continue to navigate existing data while progress is made on background analysis and/or artifact generation.

### Why?

I am working on a project where I have items in a dataframe and I can see existing artifacts regarding that data. When a add more data to the dataframe, I want to generate new artifacts associated to the new data, and possibly update the artifacts of the existing data as needed. But I don't want that background processing to hinder the review of data that is currently available and I want to review any new artifacts as they become available via the background process. And I want a progress bar that tells me how many item have been processed so far. Unfortunately, there is no way I have seen to get around the fact that st.progress blocks the main interaction and update thread.

### How?

#### Function Signatures

   - async_progress(ss_name='async_prog_bar', async_func=async_func, af_args=[af_args], af_kwargs={af_kwargs})
       - The async_progress object upon instantiation should check for existing state in the session_state object and update itself accordingly.
       - Then it should spawn an async thread within the __main__ block that periodically updates the progress bar data in the session_state object.
       - The async thread should stop if it can no-longer find it's associated data in the session_state object.
       - The async thread should also enable a url (http://localhost:9504/async/<session_id>/<element_name>) to receive update requests from an async java script that is associated to the progress bar element on the web page, which it periodically updates.
   - async_func(ss_prog_bar: str, *args, **kwargs) 
       - async_func must be async ie. 'async def async_func()'
       - async_func modifies the progress bar by referencing and updating the ss_prog_bar element the session_state object.
       - if async_func is itself generates threads, then only the main thread should update the progress bar.
       - async_func should stop if it can no-longer find it's associated progress-bar data in the session_state object.

#### async_progress annotations

   - @st.async_progress
      - Indicates that the function is an async_progress function.
      - Validates and/or sets the function to be async.

title: Fragment to fragment (co-fragment) communication instead of rerunning entire app
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Would be great to create a functionality for co-fragment communication directly rather than re-running the entire app. This could be streamlit's blockhain moment - no middle men (in this case the entire app).

### Why?

Re-rendering the entire app for co-fragment communication is frustration slow. Co-fragment communication would drastically increase the speed and performance of a streamlit app. 

### How?

My app looks like the below:

![fragments](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f5e0ea57-452c-4696-89c2-112ac27dd9b2)

The black outlines are fragments. The purple/pink outlines are nested fragments. I understand co-fragment communication occurs through session_state which is great but for this communication to be recognised, one must re-run the whole app. This makes the app more slow and somewhat buggy in my experience of operating my app. 

Seeing as fragments can be re-run periodically, it would be great to add the possibility to communicate between specific fragments via an action. For example, in my app image, After I input details in the "Contact Details" expander, I want to update the CV Preview fragment. But to do that, I have to re-run the entire app. Perhaps the possibility to rerun specific fragments based on some unique Id (like a key of a streamlit widget) when I say click on the submit form button in the Contact Details expander would be great. 

Just an example
```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"])
```

The issue with the above is for every rerun action, the `keys to update` will rerun. So perhaps, we could create a trigger command parameter.

```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=["form_submit_btn"])
```

We could also get fancy and connect trigger keys to keys to update:


```
@st.fragment(key="test_frag", keys_to_update=["frag1", "frag2"], trigger_keys=[{"frag1":"form_submit_btn"}])
```

title: Support Multi-Tenant Folder Structure for Built-In Pages Navigation
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

Currently, Streamlit automatically generates a sidebar navigation based on the scripts in a pages/ folder. I’d like to extend this to support tenant-based folders, so that each authenticated user (tenant) sees only the pages within their designated folder. This would enable a seamless multi-tenant dashboard structure within a single Streamlit app.

### Why?

1. Multi-Tenant Support: In many SaaS scenarios, each tenant (or client/project) has unique pages or dashboards.
2. Scalability: Storing tenant-specific pages in dedicated folders would keep the codebase organized, while reusing common components across tenants.
3. Security & Personalization: Automatically generating the correct sidebar for each tenant ensures that users only see content relevant to their role or tenant.

### How?

- Extended Pages Folder: Introduce an optional directory structure such as:
        tenants/
          --tenant1/
            ----page1.py
            ---- page2.py
          --tenant2/
            ----page1.py
            ----page2.py
- Automatic Side Nav: Streamlit would detect these sub-folders at runtime (similar to how it currently handles pages/) and generate a tenant-specific navigation based on authentication or session state.
- Role/Tenant Check: When a user logs in, Streamlit could read a tenant or role from st.session_state and render pages from the corresponding tenant folder only.
- Optional Config: Perhaps a parameter or config setting in config.toml (e.g., multi_tenant = true) that, when enabled, triggers this multi-folder scanning and nav generation.

title: Expose OAuth errors during `st.login`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

We're soon launching native authentication in Streamlit (see #8518). One thing we left out for now is handling errors that appear during the OAuth flow. It would be great to either handle them automatically (e.g. by showing a dialog or toast) or exposing them programmatically. 



### Why?

These errors should be very rare in Streamlit because many errors are handled directly in the OAuth flow by the identity provider and [most possible errors that are propagated back to the app](https://www.oauth.com/oauth2-servers/server-side-apps/possible-errors/) are due to a) wrong configuration (which we usually catch before even initiating the OAuth flow), b) wrong implementation (which we control), or c) the server of the identity provider being down (which shouldn't happen often for the major providers). 

But errors can still happen – the most prominent example we found during testing is when the user clicks "Cancel" on the consent screen shown when logging in for the first time. And there might be others we didn't think about yet. 

### How?

Two possible ways:

1. Automatically show a dialog or toast with the error code and potentially error description and error URI. Note that OAuth recommends showing a custom error message to the user instead of showing the error code and error description directly. But I think in our case (where these errors are very rare), it might be fine to just show that and not require the developer to implement it themselves. We should probably have a parameter on `st.login` to disable this automatic notification in case the developer wants to handle the error themselves (see 2). 
2. Expose the error details programmatically. One way would be to put it into `st.user` as keys `error`, `error_description` (optional), and `error_uri` (optional). In that case, we should automatically clear these items on the next rerun, otherwise it becomes very hard to only show the error when it happens. Another possible approach would be to have an `on_error` callback on `st.login`. But a) we'd need to pass the error details to this callback, which would make it work a bit differently than our callbacks (currently) work and b) it's a bit more cumbersome to work with this in practice because you often have to stick the error message into `st.session_state` if you want to show it somewhere within the app. 

### Additional Context

Introduce `st.set_page_title` or a similar method of changing the page title. This should work as, in my understanding, the reason why `st.set_page_config` is blocked from running later in the app lifecycle is due to layout, not the title.

### Additional Context

Some (e.g. https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/2216) have suggested using the st.session_state to push the title. In my case this does not work, as new app pages are opened as new tabs, loosing the session_state.
